info.title: Propel MBOM API
info.summary: Create, read, edit, baseline and reconcile a Manufacturing BOM.
info.description:
The complete REST surface of Propel's Manufacturing BOM (MBOM), built on the new
**branch / baseline / configuration-item** framework. Eight endpoints cover the whole
lifecycle: create an MBOM over a released eBOM revision, read its structure, edit it with
delta operations, freeze it as a baseline, and reconcile it against a newer eBOM revision.

---

## Read this first: the eight ideas the whole API rests on

### 1. An MBOM inherits its structure. It never copies it.

Creating an MBOM writes **four records and not one row of BOM structure**. The branch stores
only its own *deltas*; everything else is resolved at read time by walking the live legacy
`Assembly__c` graph beneath the accepted eBOM root revision. An untouched branch holds zero
per-edge records however many times it is read.

### 2. `T_R` — the pinned source clock

When an MBOM is created (or a pull is committed), the accepted root revision's
**release date** is stamped once as `Source_TimePoint__c`. That timestamp is **T_R**, and every
`base` row resolves against it: a child item renders at whichever revision was released as
of T_R.

T_R is *stamped, then read* — never re-derived. So when engineering releases `Assy-100` rev-2,
**nothing happens to the MBOM**. It still resolves against rev-1's T_R until someone explicitly
accepts the newer revision with a [pull](#tag/Pull).

### 3. `asOf` — the branch clock, and why there are two

Every read also takes an `asOf` timestamp (defaulting to now). That one governs the *branch's*
own content — its deltas, its locally added parts, its substitutes.

Two clocks are therefore legitimately in play at once, and each row states which one governs it
(`TreeRowDTO.governingTimestamp`, `MemberState.governingClock`):

| Row kind | Governing clock |
|---|---|
| `base` — supplied by the source, untouched | **T_R** (`source`) |
| `claiming` — the branch took copy-on-write ownership of a source row | **`asOf`** (`branch`) for its quantity and find number |
| `new` — branch-owned, no upstream provenance | **`asOf`** (`branch`) |
| a *substitute* (from `replace`) | **`asOf`** — its child floats |

A direct consequence is that **one item can render at two different revisions in the same
tree**. That is expected, not a fault, and is reported as a `MIXED_REVISION` warning beside the
data rather than an error instead of it.

#### A third answer: a chosen revision (MVP-30357)

A row's **child revision** can also be the caller's explicit choice rather than any clock's
output. Every operation that creates or takes over a row (`claim`, `add`, `replace`,
`convert-to-native`) accepts a `childItemRevisionId`; a row that stores one is **pinned** and
renders exactly that revision whatever T_R or `asOf` say.
(**🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** `set-revision` changes or clears it
afterwards.) A row that stores none
**tracks**:

| Row | Stored revision | Child revision it renders |
|---|---|---|
| tracking claim (`trackChildRevision: true`) | none | the source line's own, at **T_R** — it moves when a pull accepts a newer source |
| `new` row / substitute, no revision sent | none | whatever is released at **`asOf`** (floats) |
| tracking convert (`trackChildRevision: true`) | none | floats at **`asOf`**, like an `add` — it has no source left to follow |
| any pinned row | `childItemRevisionId` | the pin, always |

`claim` and `convert-to-native` have no default and must say which they want — see the
[delta endpoint](#operation/applyDeltaBatch). A row pinned to a revision **other than** the one
its source line resolves to renders that revision's own structure beneath it, read-only, in
place of the source's lines.

### 4. Provenance: `base` / `claiming` / `new`

Derived at read time, never stored. `claiming` and `new` differ by exactly one field on the
winning delta row (`Claims_Source__c` set vs. null), and that difference is what makes
"what did I change relative to upstream?" answerable. A fourth value, `nested`, marks the
read-only rows beneath a locally added or substituted assembly, or beneath a pinned row.

*Renamed in MVP-30309 — these were `inherited` / `claimed` / `local` before.*

### 5. Copy-on-write: you must `claim` before you can edit

A `base` row is read-only. Editing it is refused with `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, carrying the eBOM
line id so the client can offer the claim. Divergence from upstream is always an explicit act.
(**🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** `update` with `autoClaim: true` claims and
revises in one operation. It is still explicit, and the result reports `claimed: true`.)

### 6. Nothing is ever deleted

Removal is an **exclude delta** — a tombstone appended to an append-only log. `restore` lifts
it. A hard delete of any branch-owned row is refused (`HARD_DELETE_BLOCKED`). This is what makes
a read at a past `asOf`, and therefore a baseline, reproducible.

### 7. A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

Cutting a baseline records one timestamp and freezes the revisions it resolved to. Reading it
**re-resolves** the branch at that timestamp. Two stored counts act as canaries if something the
resolution depends on has moved since — `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` for the row count, and
`BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` for how many of those rows are the branch's own claims.
(**🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** A third, `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT`, for how many
rows hold an explicitly chosen revision.)

### 8. "Pull", not "merge"

A pull is the **downstream-initiated acceptance of a newer upstream source version**, matching
`Branch_Source__c.Source_Type__c`. The word *merge* is deliberately reserved for the Phase 2
branch-to-branch operation, which is bidirectional and common-ancestor-based — genuinely
different.

---

## Response and error conventions

These conventions differ from other Propel REST endpoints:

- Success and error bodies are **plain JSON, never wrapped** in an
  `entity` / `entities` envelope.
- **Error bodies key the code as `code`, not `errorCode`.** `errorCode` appears in this API only
  *inside* a delta batch's per-operation `results[]`.
- **Nulls are not suppressed.** A field left null for that case is meaningfully null — see
  `DeltaResult.forked`, where `null` and `false` say different things.
- **The code is the contract; the message is not.** Messages are translated. Switch on `code`,
  never on text.

### Status-code scheme

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **400** | The request could not be read, or a value is out of range. Fix the request. |
| **403** | No permission. The body carries the label only — never the object that was denied. |
| **404** | The path, or an id in the body, names nothing. |
| **409** | Well formed, and **retryable after changing state** — claim it first, restore it first, re-preview. |
| **413** | More than 200 operations in one delta batch. |
| **422** | Well formed, but **impossible against the model**. Retrying unchanged will never succeed (a cycle is still a cycle). |
| **500** | Unmodelled server failure. Carries the exception type and message, never the stack trace. |

The 409/422 split is deliberate: a client that retries on a generic 4xx would spin forever on a
cycle, and the two cases want different UI.

---

## Design intent: MBOM-specific paths, generic vocabulary

MBOM is the first application of a general branch / baseline / configuration-item framework. The
path is namespaced under `/mbom` so MBOM-only rules have somewhere to live, but the nouns below
that segment — **branch**, **source**, **member**, **claim**, **baseline** — are framework
concepts, not MBOM concepts. Everything MBOM-specific is confined to a single discriminated
schema, `AssemblyEdgeDetail`, reached through `MemberState.detail` and keyed by `ciKind`. A
second configuration-item type adds a sibling schema there and touches nothing else.

## Paths

There is **no `branchId` path segment on the source endpoints**: a source already names its
owning branch. `branchId` still appears in the pull-preview *body*, denormalised for display.

---

## Planned changes (not yet implemented)

This version of the contract also describes tickets that are **designed but not built**, so
their test cases can be written ahead of the code. Nothing below is live yet:

- Every planned operation, schema, property or parameter carries
  `x-planned: { ticket, assumptions }`, and its description opens with
  **🚧 Planned — MVP-xxxxx, not yet implemented.**
- A planned value added to an existing enum is listed in the enum. The enum's description
  has a `Value | Status` table saying which values are planned.
- Behaviour changes to existing elements are called out inline with the same banner.
- Where a ticket left a design question open, the answer assumed here is recorded in the
  assumptions ledger, `docs/architecture/cm/cm-api-planned-assumptions.md` (PLM repo), under
  an ID like `A-30378-2`. Each passage that depends on an answer cites its ID.
- Each planned example shows **only its own ticket's surface**. Other tickets' planned fields
  are left out, so an example still matches its ticket if that ticket ships alone. Once
  several have shipped, a real response carries all of their fields (for example, a
  `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` tree also carries `isPinned`).

When a ticket ships, remove its markers: grep for its key.

| Ticket | Surface it adds or changes |
|---|---|
| [MVP-30375](https://propelplm.atlassian.net/browse/MVP-30375) | `TreeRow.isPinned` and `TreeRow.wasClaimed` on every tree read. `TreeRow.pinnedById` / `pinnedAt` on baseline rows. A `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` warning on the baseline read. |
| [MVP-30376](https://propelplm.atlassian.net/browse/MVP-30376) | A `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` warning on the branch tree read, one per row whose chosen revision is now Cancelled or Expired. The revision still renders. |
| [MVP-30377](https://propelplm.atlassian.net/browse/MVP-30377) | `DeltaOperation.autoClaim` on `update`, which claims and revises a `base` edge in one operation and carries the same revision choice as `claim`. `DeltaResult.claimed` reports it. |
| [MVP-30378](https://propelplm.atlassian.net/browse/MVP-30378) | A `set-revision` delta op that sets, changes or clears a stored child revision, with clearing spelled `trackChildRevision: true`. An optional `accept-source-revision` pull action on a retargeted `claim-retained` entry. `DiffEntry.revisionAdvances`. `update` refuses a `childItemRevisionId`, and `update` / `set-revision` reach a row hidden behind a pin by `assemblyCiId`. |
| [MVP-30379](https://propelplm.atlassian.net/browse/MVP-30379) | Per-field pull decisions: `PullCommitRequest.decisions[].acceptedFields`, with `candidate` / `release` per field. Optional `accept-fields` on `claim-retained` and `member-add-collision`, and `release` on `claim-superseded`. `claim-orphaned` stays the only required decision. |

post.summary: Create an MBOM over a released eBOM revision
post.description:
Creates an MBOM header, its first branch, the branch's eBOM source lineage, and that
source's first acceptance — **four records in one transaction, and zero rows of BOM
structure**.

The response returns all four ids rather than just `mbomId`, because a caller that had to go
looking for the other three would be querying schema this API exists to hide. The one you
will use most is `sourceId` — it is the `sourceId` every `/sources/...` endpoint
takes.

## The root revision must be Released

Its `Released_Date_Time__c` becomes **T_R**, the timepoint every `base` row resolves at.
An unreleased revision has no such date, so there is nothing to pin to.

Four shapes are refused with `NOT_RELEASED` (409, not 400 — releasing the revision makes the
identical request succeed): not released; **Cancelled**; **Expired**; released but carrying
no release date. Cancelled and Expired are excluded because the eBOM's own as-of read would
never resolve them either.

## Timestamps stamped here

| Field | Value | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `Source_TimePoint__c` (**T_R**) | the root revision's release date | what `base` rows resolve at, forever |
| `Accepted_At__c` | the **wall clock**, now | which acceptance governs a given `asOf` |

A consequence worth knowing before you write a test: because `Accepted_At__c` is the wall
clock, a branch created now renders **nothing** when read at an `asOf` in the past. That is
the acceptance not existing yet at that timestamp, not a defect.

## Access

Gated **before the body is read**: a caller with no create grant gets 403 whatever they sent.
Requires create on `MBOM__c`, `Branch__c`, `Branch_Source__c` and
`Branch_Source_Rev__c`, plus read on `Item_Revision__c`. All five are named so a partial
grant is a clean 403 rather than a 500 out of the middle of the DML.

201.description:
Created. Four records now exist. 201 rather than 200 because the response names records
that did not exist before the call, and a client distinguishing "created" from "already
there" has nothing else to read.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — the body was empty or unreadable; `mbomName` or `branchLabel` was
blank; or either exceeded its field length (`mbomName` ≤ 80, `branchLabel` ≤ 80 — the
shorter of `Branch__c.Name` at 80 and `Label__c` at 255).

A malformed id in the **body** is a 400 while one in the **URI** is a 404, and that is
not an inconsistency: the URI is what *names* the resource, so a path naming nothing is
a path to nothing. A body field is a value in a request to a resource that does exist.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (mbomName is required)

404.description:
`NOT_FOUND` — `rootItemRevisionId` was null, is not an `Item_Revision__c` id, or names
no visible row. The three are not distinguished on purpose: separating "malformed" from
"absent" would tell an unauthorised caller which ids exist.

value.message: That record does not exist, or you do not have access to it. (a0Bg8000000Ab10EAC is not an Item_Revision__c)

409.description:
`NOT_RELEASED` — the root revision is unreleased, Cancelled, Expired, or has no release
date, so there is no T_R to stamp.

value.message: An mBOM can only be created from a released item revision. (a0Ag8000000Ab99EAC)

get.description:
The branch's resolved content at one timepoint: the eBOM traversed at **T_R**, with the
branch's own deltas folded and overlaid at **`asOf`**.

This is the main read. It is where the two-clock model becomes visible — every row states
its own `provenance` and its own `governingTimestamp`, because a row that did not carry its
own clock would be unexplainable to the person looking at it.

## What the response contains that you might not expect

- **Excluded rows are rendered**, carrying `isExcluded: true`. A tree read shows the person
  editing what was removed. (A *baseline* read filters them out — see that endpoint.)
- **`isEditable: false`** on any row inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted
  assembly, or of a **pinned** row. Only content the branch's *source* supplied can be
  claimed or changed. It is stated rather than left to be derived from `provenance`, so a
  client does not have to encode which provenance values happen to be editable this
  release. Every delta op refuses these rows (`NOT_EDITABLE`), so a UI offering an action on
  one is offering an action the API will reject.
- **A pinned row renders its own revision's structure.** A row whose chosen
  `childItemRevisionId` differs from the revision its source line resolves to at T_R gets
  that revision's eBOM beneath it as read-only `nested` rows, and the source's lines under
  it are suppressed. A branch edit sitting on one of those suppressed lines — a claim,
  exclusion, update or substitute, or an `add` under an item only the suppressed structure
  supplied — takes no effect, and the read says so with `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`
  rather than failing.
- **Each occurrence renders its own structure (MVP-30214).** One item can render in two
  places at two revisions — one occurrence pinned and another still at the source's
  revision, or two pins. Each occurrence follows its own revision: a pinned occurrence
  renders that revision's `nested` rows beneath it, and an unpinned occurrence keeps the
  source's lines. An edit on a suppressed line is hidden only when no occurrence still
  renders that line, and `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` then names every pinned revision
  that hid it. `MIXED_REVISION` still fires, never blocking. A branch `add` under such an
  item binds to the item, not to one rendering: it appears under **every** occurrence,
  with no warning of its own, and survives the parent advancing to a newer revision. No
  field is added to the row. The occurrences themselves are told apart by `edgeKey` and
  `detail.parentItemId`; their children are not, in the flat shape (see below).
- **A substitute never absorbs another line of its new child (MVP-30214).** When a
  `replace` substitute's child item also has its own, unrelated eBOM line under the same
  parent, both render. The substitute is its own row with its own
  `replaces-{branchId}-{supersededEdgeKey}-{newChildItemId}` key, and the other line keeps
  its own row and `edgeKey`. The ambiguous position match is declined rather than refused,
  so this read never answers `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION`. If upstream later makes the same
  substitution itself, two rows render — the substitute beside upstream's new line —
  rather than one.
- **🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** **Every row says whether its revision was a
  choice.** `isPinned` is true exactly when the row stores a chosen child revision. A
  clock-resolved row that happens to resolve to the same revision is `false`. `wasClaimed`
  marks a `new` row that `convert-to-native` flipped from `claiming`. Both follow the
  explicit decision, not the structural pin above. [assumes A-30375-1, A-30375-2]
- **🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** **A dead chosen revision is warned about,
  never replaced.** A row whose stored `childItemRevisionId` has since been Cancelled or
  Expired still renders that revision, and the read raises one `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`
  per such row. This read is the only one that raises it. [assumes A-30376-2, A-30376-3]
- **Unreachable rows are dropped.** A delta can name a parent item that is not in the tree —
  a subassembly whose item had nothing released at T_R drops out, and a claim beneath it
  survives the overlay as a row with an absent parent. This read walks down from the root and
  keeps only what it can reach, in **both** shapes.
- **`warnings` and `rows` are always present**, empty rather than absent. A client that has
  to distinguish "no warnings" from "the key is missing" writes null checks at every call
  site, and one of them is eventually forgotten.

## Flat vs. nested, and a real trap

`flat=true` (the **default**) returns one row per edge, each carrying `detail.parentItemId` and an
empty `childRows` — losslessly re-nestable by the client. `flat=false` nests via `childRows`.

The one exception is an item that renders at two revisions, each occurrence with its own
structure (above). The children of both occurrences name the same `parentItemId`, and a
flat row does not say which revision's line it is, so re-nesting by `parentItemId` hangs
every occurrence's children under each. Read such a tree with `flat=false`, which places
each row under the occurrence it belongs to.

**The nested shape duplicates a shared subassembly; the flat shape does not.** The traversal
walks a DAG and emits a shared subtree once; nesting re-materialises it under every parent
that uses it, because that is what a BOM tree looks like to a person expanding it. So the two
shapes carry the same *content* but not the same row **count** — never treat a nested row
count as a total — and a deeply shared DAG can hit heap nested while rendering comfortably
flat.

## Reads create nothing

No DML anywhere on this path. An untouched branch stays at zero rows however many times it
is read.

400.description:
`ASOF_INVALID` — `asOf` could not be parsed. `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — `asOf` is later than now;
there is no configuration at a timepoint that has not happened.

value.message: The timepoint could not be read. Use an ISO-8601 timestamp, for example 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z. (yesterday)

422.description:
`EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM itself contains a cycle, so its structure cannot be
resolved. Fix the eBOM; retrying is pointless.

get.summary: Read what a source supplies, with no branch deltas applied
get.description:
The "**what would I inherit?**" read: the structure as one source supplies it, with the
branch's claims, excludes and replaces deliberately **not** overlaid.

Use it to answer "what did I change relative to upstream?" by diffing this against
`GET /mbom/branches/{branchId}/tree`. Every row comes back `provenance: base`.

## Why there is no `flat` parameter

A source's own structure has no deltas overlaid on it, so there is no nesting decision to
make. An unexpected `flat` is **ignored rather than rejected**, so one parameter set can be
sent to both tree reads.

400.description: `ASOF_INVALID` or `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — see the branch tree read.

422.description: `EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM contains a cycle.

post.summary: Apply a batch of delta operations to a branch
post.description:
The single write endpoint for editing a branch. Eight operations — `claim`, `update`, `add`,
`exclude`, `restore`, `replace`, `revert`, `convert-to-native` — arrive in one array and are
applied under one envelope. (**🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** A ninth,
`set-revision`.)

**Returns `200`, not `201`**, even though rows are created: the response is a *report* on a
set of operations, not a pointer to one new resource, and under `atomic: false` some of them
may have failed.

## How a batch executes

1. **Size check** — more than 200 operations is `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before
   anything is resolved.
2. **One snapshot.** The branch is resolved **once**, at `asOf`. That is the whole reason a
   batch endpoint exists: twenty operations resolving the branch each would be twenty
   traversals, and the tree could shift underneath the batch halfway through.
3. **Validate everything, then apply.** Two passes, never interleaved, so *every* fault is
   reported rather than only the first.
4. **Persist** in a fixed number of DML statements — twenty claims cost the same statements
   as one.

### Order is preserved, but order is not sequencing

Results come back in request order with your `clientRef` echoed and `index` stated. But
**every operation validates against the one pre-batch snapshot, so a later operation cannot
see an earlier one's effect.** `[claim(L), update(L)]` in one batch answers `CLAIM_REQUIRED`
on the update — and under the default `atomic: true` that rejects the whole batch.

> **Dependent edits are two requests, not two operations.**

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** The most common dependent pair, claim then
> change a quantity, becomes **one** operation:
> `{"op": "update", "ebomAssemblyId": "…", "quantity": 3, "autoClaim": true, "trackChildRevision": true}`.
> The batch still does not sequence, so `[claim(L), update(L)]` still answers
> `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. [assumes A-30377-1]

## `atomic` — the failure contract is yours to choose

| `atomic` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `true` (**default** — a null wins the safer contract) | All-or-nothing. Any validation failure throws: the status is the **first failure's** own code (so a batch whose only fault is `CLAIM_REQUIRED` still answers 409, not a generic 400) and the body carries a `failures[]` array with **every** failure. The branch is left exactly as it was. |
| `false` | Apply what is valid, report the rest. `200` with per-operation `results[]`. |

`atomic: false` reports per-operation **validation** failures only. It does not fall back to
per-operation DML: the aggregate is one savepoint and one set of statements, and a failure
there rolls the batch back and propagates.

## `asOf` chooses what a batch *validates* against; it never dates the write

Every row written is effective **now**, whatever `asOf` says. A past `asOf` means "validate
against the configuration as it stood then" — optimistic concurrency, not time travel.
Backdating the write would let a batch win the current fold *and* change what a read at an
intervening timestamp returned, rewriting history in an append-only log.

Several operations therefore **refuse a past `asOf` outright** with `INVALID_REQUEST`,
because they decide from the branch's *current* state: `restore`, `revert`,
`convert-to-native`, and any `claim` / `add` / `exclude` / `replace` that has to mint a new
edge identity.

## `Idempotency-Key`

Read and passed through, and **ignored this phase**. It is accepted so a client can start
sending it now without its first request failing, and a later phase can honour it without a
breaking change.

## The operations

| `op` | Required fields | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `ebomAssemblyId`, and **exactly one of** `childItemRevisionId` \| `trackChildRevision: true` | Takes one live eBOM line into the branch as a copy-on-write claim, so the branch can diverge from it. Copies quantity and find number as they stand; the child revision is the caller's choice — a chosen revision **pins** it, `trackChildRevision: true` **tracks** the source line at T_R. Writes 5 records. |
| `update` | `assemblyCiId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId`; `quantity` and/or `findNumber` | Revises a branch-owned edge. Edits its `CI_Rev__c` in place while Draft; otherwise allocates a new revision, freezes the old one, and returns `forked: true`. Membership is not touched. |
| `add` | `parentItemId`, `childItemId`, `quantity`, `findNumber`; optional `childItemRevisionId` | Adds a part the eBOM never supplied — packaging, fixtures, consumables. Provenance `new`: `Claims_Source__c` stays null. The child **floats** at `asOf`, unless `childItemRevisionId` pins it. |
| `exclude` | `ebomAssemblyId` **or** `ciId` | Tombstones a row. **No cascade is written** — the descendant prune is computed at read time, because a descendant still supplied through another path must survive. |
| `restore` | `ciId` | Lifts an exclusion. Appends `Add` when the branch holds content for the row, or `Revert` when it does not (a `base` row excluded straight from a stub) — appending `Add` blindly would break the next read. |
| `replace` | `replacedEbomAssemblyId`, `newChildItemId`, `quantity`, `findNumber`; optional `childItemRevisionId` | Substitutes a different child for the one an eBOM line supplies, **recording that it is a substitution** (`Replaces__c`), so the pair does not read as an unrelated removal plus an unrelated addition. The substitute floats at `asOf` unless `childItemRevisionId` pins it. |
| `revert` | `ciId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId` | Discards the branch's claim so the row falls back to what its source supplies. Nothing on disk is touched — a `Revert` marker is appended and the fold drops it entirely. |
| `convert-to-native` | `ciId`, and **exactly one of** `childItemRevisionId` \| `trackChildRevision: true` | Severs a claiming edge's link to the source it claims: same quantity and find number, but now branch-owned in its own right (`provenance` flips `claiming` → `new`). Appends an `Add` with `Claims_Source__c` null; the child revision is the caller's choice — a chosen revision is stamped on, `trackChildRevision: true` floats at `asOf`. |

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** A ninth operation:
>
> | `op` | Required fields | What it does |
> |---|---|---|
> | `set-revision` | `assemblyCiId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId`, and **exactly one of** `childItemRevisionId` \| `trackChildRevision: true` | Sets, changes or **clears** a branch-owned row's stored child revision, keeping its quantity and find number. It always appends a new `CI_Rev__c` and never edits one in place. A `childItemRevisionId` **pins** the row. `trackChildRevision: true` **clears** the pin, and what the row then follows depends on the row. A cleared claim becomes a tracking claim: it renders its source line's revision at T_R and moves only when a pull accepts a newer source. A cleared `new` row or substitute floats at `asOf`. Setting a pin that differs from the source line's revision starts rendering that revision's structure beneath the row. Clearing it, or setting it back to the source line's revision, stops that, and any edits it hid render again. |
>
> It refuses the following, in this order:
>
> 1. `INVALID_REQUEST`: no id.
> 2. `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`: neither or both choice fields.
> 3. `NOT_FOUND`
> 4. `NOT_EDITABLE`: a nested row.
> 5. `NOT_SUPPLIED`: a tombstone.
> 6. `CLAIM_REQUIRED`: a row that is still `base`. There is nothing to store a revision on
>    until the branch owns the row.
> 7. `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`
>
> Sending the revision the row already stores succeeds and writes nothing. `forked` is
> always null. A past `asOf` is tolerated, as on `update`.
> [assumes A-30378-1, A-30378-2, A-30378-8, A-30378-9]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** `set-revision` also takes an optional
> `quantity` and `findNumber`, applied partially as on `update`. One operation can then
> change a row's revision and its quantity together, which is what a pull's
> `accept-fields` compiles to when it accepts both. Restating the stored revision then
> writes nothing only if the quantity and find number are unchanged too (A-30378-8).
> [assumes A-30379-5]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** `update` gains an optional
> `autoClaim: true`. With it, the operation also needs **exactly one of**
> `childItemRevisionId` | `trackChildRevision: true`, and an update of a `base` edge claims
> and revises in one operation instead of answering `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. The result says so
> with `claimed: true`. See `DeltaOperation.autoClaim`. [assumes A-30377-1, A-30377-2]

### Choosing a child revision (MVP-30357)

A stored revision must always mean somebody chose it, so the operations that create or take
over a row treat `childItemRevisionId` as a deliberate choice, never a default:

| `op` | `childItemRevisionId` sent | `trackChildRevision: true` sent | Neither | Both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claim` | **pins** the claimed row to it | row **tracks** the source line — the revision its unclaimed self would render, at T_R, moving when a pull accepts a newer source | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| `convert-to-native` | **stamped** onto the native row | nothing stored; the native row **floats** at `asOf`, like an `add` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| `add`, `replace` | **pins** the new row / substitute | ignored — blank already means track | the row **floats** at `asOf` (the default) | pins; the flag is ignored |
| 🚧 MVP-30377: `update` with `autoClaim: true`, on a `base` edge | claims and **pins** | claims and **tracks** | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| 🚧 MVP-30377: `update` with `autoClaim: true`, on an owned edge | accepted if equal to the stored revision, else `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming `set-revision` | ignored | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| every other op | ignored | ignored | — | — |

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** The two `update` rows above are
> planned. [assumes A-30377-1]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Two more rows change:
>
> | `op` | `childItemRevisionId` sent | `trackChildRevision: true` sent | Neither | Both |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | `set-revision` | **sets or changes** the pin | **clears** it | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
> | `update` (without `autoClaim`) | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming `set-revision`, where today it is silently ignored | ignored | — | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` |
>
> [assumes A-30378-2, A-30378-6]

- **There is no server-side "pin what I see".** To pin the revision the tree is showing, or
  to have a convert "keep what it shows", send back that row's own
  `detail.childItemRevisionId`. That includes converting a *pinned* claim that should stay
  pinned: nothing is retained implicitly.
- **The revision must belong to the row's child item** — for `claim`, the claimed line's
  child; for `replace`, the substitute; for `convert-to-native`, the converted row's.
  Otherwise `422 REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`. A revision you cannot see answers the same code
  as one that does not exist, so the check is not an existence oracle. Lifecycle
  (Cancelled / Expired) is **not** screened at write time.
  **🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** It is not screened at write time then
  either, because a revision can be cancelled long after it was chosen. The branch tree
  read warns about it instead (`STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`). [assumes A-30376-2]
- **Why `claim` no longer defaults.** Claiming a line to change its quantity used to pin its
  revision as a side effect, which silently also meant "never accept a new revision of
  this part" — two decisions, one of them invisible at the call site.
- **A pinned row can hide branch edits.** A pin on an assembly other than the revision its
  source line resolves to renders that revision's structure beneath it; see the
  [branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree) and `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`.
- Changing or clearing a revision after the row exists is not an operation this release
  offers.
  **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** `set-revision` changes or clears it
  and keeps the row's quantity and find number. `convert-to-native` may still stamp **any**
  revision of the child item, or switch to tracking. That is legitimate, and it is the
  severing path. `set-revision` is the non-severing one. [assumes A-30378-1, A-30378-7]

### Addressing quirks worth knowing

- `update` accepts `ebomAssemblyId` **and has to**: a `base` row has no edge record, so
  that is the only id a client holds for the row whose update must come back
  `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. Without it the rejection could never be reached.
- `revert` accepts `ebomAssemblyId` for the mirror reason: a reverted row renders with no
  `CI__c` at all, so a *second* revert — which must answer `NO_CLAIM` — cannot be
  addressed any other way.
- `replace` only works on eBOM-derived rows. A `new` row has a synthetic `new-…` edge
  key and no `Assembly__c` line, so replacing branch-added content is `update`, or
  `exclude` plus `add`.
- A row **hidden behind a pin** (see `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`) is addressable by
  `ciId` for `exclude`, `restore`, `revert` and `convert-to-native`. `update` and `claim`
  answer `NOT_FOUND` for it.
  **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** `update` and `set-revision` addressed
  by `assemblyCiId` find it too. Addressed by `ebomAssemblyId`, they still answer
  `NOT_FOUND`. `claim` of a hidden line keeps answering `NOT_FOUND`: a line that renders
  nowhere has nothing visible to claim. [assumes A-30378-5]

## Access

Requires **create** on `Assembly_CI__c`, `CI__c`, `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`, `CI_Rev__c` and
`Branch_Member__c`, **and edit** on `Assembly_CI__c` (upserted) and `CI_Rev__c` (updated when
an operation freezes a predecessor). Create and edit are not the same permission, and both
are named so a partial grant is a 403 before any DML.

post.summary: Cut a baseline over a branch
post.description:
Records the branch's full effective structure at one timepoint — **as that timepoint**.

## A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

The cut writes one `Baseline__c` carrying `Resolution_TimePoint__c`, and nothing else about
the content. Reading it back **replays the resolution** at that timestamp, which is exact
because the resolution is a pure function of it and because nothing can ever land at or
before a past T (`Accepted_At__c` and `EffectiveDateTime__c` are both stamped with the wall
clock).

The flattened member table this replaces cost one record per edge per cut — roughly 36 MB at
the measured 18,000-edge ceiling.

## The freeze is what makes the replay honest

A Draft `CI_Rev__c` is edited **in place** by `update`. Replaying a timepoint would therefore
follow an edit made *after* the cut, and the baseline would change without anyone touching
it. So the cut freezes every revision the snapshot resolved to. From then on, every `update`
to those rows forks a new revision instead (and comes back `forked: true`).

## Two timestamps, and why they are not one

`resolutionTimePoint` is what the content was resolved at; `takenAt` is the wall-clock moment
of the cut. Kept apart, a correction to the server clock cannot change what a baseline
resolves to. (MVP-30030 called both `cutDateTime`; the **request** still does, the response
does not.)

## Excluded rows are not members

`memberCount` counts what the configuration *contains*, so tombstoned rows are not counted —
which means it is **not** the number of rows the tree endpoint renders. The baseline read
filters on the same predicate, so the stored count stays comparable to a later read.

## Immutable from the insert

There is no draft-baseline state and no lock step: every update to a `Baseline__c` is refused
outright, and every hard delete too.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Baseline__c`, and **edit** on `Baseline__c` and `CI_Rev__c` (the
freeze). Named separately because a partial grant would otherwise fail half way through the
cut — after the members resolve and before the freeze, the one state a baseline must never
be left in.

`ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — `cutDateTime` is later than now; a baseline of content that does not
exist yet is not a baseline. `ASOF_INVALID` — it could not be parsed.

get.summary: Read the rows a baseline captured
get.description:
Re-resolves the branch at the baseline's stored `Resolution_TimePoint__c` and returns the
rows.

## `asOf` is refused, not ignored

Every other tree read on this API takes one, and a client that has been sending it to
`/branches/{id}/tree` will send it here. A baseline **pins its own timepoint**, so a second
one has nothing to answer — accepting it would give the same rows to every value and let a
caller believe they had asked a temporal question and got a temporal answer. Sending `asOf`
is a `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

`flat` **is** honoured, because that is a shape and not a clock.

## Differences from the branch read

- **Excluded rows are filtered out.** A tree read renders a tombstone so the editor can see
  what was removed; a baseline is the record of what the branch *contained*.
- **`edgeId` and `edgeKey` are suppressed, and the per-row governing clock is collapsed** —
  every row's `governingTimestamp` is the baseline's own `resolutionTimePoint`, never null. A
  baseline row does not pretend to answer questions it cannot. `isReplaced` **is**
  populated: leaving it null would render a substituted part identically to an ordinary one.
- **`warnings` carries drift only.** A `MIXED_REVISION` or `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`
  warning is advice about a branch someone is still editing; a baseline is a record of a
  decision already taken, so neither is forwarded.
- **Pinned rows reproduce exactly.** A row pinned to another revision re-resolves with that
  revision's `nested` structure beneath it and the source's lines suppressed, just as the
  branch read rendered it at the cut (MVP-30357). Before that, a baseline recorded the pin
  over the source revision's children.
- **🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** **Pinned rows name who pinned them.** A row
  with `isPinned: true` carries `pinnedById` and `pinnedAt`, taken from the payload
  revision that carries its current value. The branch read leaves both null.
  [assumes A-30375-4]

## The drift canaries

| warningCode | What moved |
|---|---|
| `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` | the baseline re-derived a **different number of rows** than its cut recorded — a corrected release date, an edit to an already-released BOM |
| `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` | the same rows came back with a **different number of them `claiming`** — a claim severed or added since the cut. The row count cannot see this, because severing one moves no row |
| `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` | **🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** The same rows came back with a **different number of them explicitly pinned** (`isPinned`). A revision decision moved where neither the row count nor the claim count did. [assumes A-30375-5] |

Both **warn rather than throw**: the rows returned are still the honest answer for the
stored timepoint. Each comparison is skipped when the cut never recorded its counter, so a
baseline taken before a counter existed does not warn on every read.

Neither is complete, and the response does not pretend otherwise. A same-second revision of
a claiming row's quantity moves no count on either axis, and an edit to a `base` line's
own fields moves none either. Both gaps have one cause — a whole-second `Datetime` used as
the fold's boundary — and closing it needs a monotonic log position rather than a third
counter.

get.summary: Preview the effect of accepting a newer eBOM revision
get.description:
Diffs the eBOM resolved at the source's current T_R against the eBOM resolved at the
candidate root revision's release date, and returns every difference as an individually
addressable entry.

**This call is pure.** It creates and modifies nothing — no `Branch_Member__c`, no
`CI_Rev__c`, no source revision. Calling it twice with the same inputs against an unchanged
org returns identical entries, including identical `entryId` values and an identical
`diffFingerprint`. Only the read clock moves: `generatedAt`, and the `governingTimestamp` of
every state that answers to `asOf`.

**Not every entry is a decision.** Most are informational: the caller is being told what will
happen, not asked. Only `claim-orphaned` blocks a commit.

**Already current is not an error.** If the branch already resolves against the newest
released root revision, this returns `200` with `hasChanges: false` and an empty `entries`
array — correct for a read, where a write would throw.

## The correlation key — why a pull doesn't orphan every claim on every release

The two traversals are correlated on **`(Parent_Item__c, Item__c, Secondary_Unique_Key__c)`**
— the legacy `Assembly__c.Tree_Unique__c` with the parent *revision* swapped for the parent
*item*. **Not** on `Assembly_CI__c.Edge_Key__c`.

This is the load-bearing decision of the whole feature. When a parent item revs, Propel
clones its entire BOM into new `Assembly__c` rows with new ids — so a branch that claimed a
line under rev-1 holds a line id that does not exist under rev-2. A join on `Edge_Key__c`
would orphan every claimed edge and re-add every upstream line **on every single pull**. The
parent item does not move when its revision does, which is exactly what lets this key survive
the clone. `Edge_Key__c` still identifies the edge *for display*; it just is not the join key.

`Secondary_Unique_Key__c` rather than `Find_Number__c` because find-number uniqueness is org
configuration, and a key built on it would give two orgs with identical data different diffs.

The key is **not unique** on one side when a parent item renders at two revisions in the
same tree, which is routine now that each occurrence of a pinned item renders its own
revision's structure (MVP-30214). `ItemCloneBatch` preserves `Secondary_Unique_Key__c`, so
both revisions' copies of a line share one key. So within one side, edges at one key are
also told apart by their **parent revision**, the revision whose line each sits on, and a
pull over such a tree completes. The parent revision separates; it never joins, and it is
not part of the key: a branch edge and its source counterpart carry different parent
revisions once the source advances. Across the sides, edges at one key pair by equal
parent revision first, and then a lone edge left on each side pairs with the other — the
source advancing. There is no tie-break on find number.

A `replace` substitute borrows the key of the line it supersedes. Where it meets a line of
its new child under the same parent revision, it stands aside rather than colliding: it is
reported on its own, as `claim-orphaned` like any live substitute without a counterpart,
and the line pairs as usual.

Where the join still cannot tell which upstream line corresponds to which branch line, the
pull answers `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` (422) rather than guess. The three shapes that raise
it, and their remedies, are listed under the 422 response.

## The two sides are deliberately asymmetric

- **current** — the branch resolved at the accepted T_R, *with* its own deltas overlaid.
- **candidate** — the **raw** upstream walk at the candidate T_R, with **no overlay at all**.

Overlaying the branch onto the candidate side would match nothing (the deltas are keyed on
line ids that do not exist under the new root) and would append every delta as an unmatched
local edge — which **resurrects the orphans**, correlating a claim on a removed line with the
branch's own edge so `claim-orphaned` is never raised. That entry is the only required
decision in the entire feature; silently losing it would make a commit that should block
succeed.

## Entry kinds

| kind | decision | availableActions | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source-version-advance` | informational | — | The root item revision advances; nothing structural beneath it changed. |
| `member-version-advance` | informational | — | An edge's child resolves to a newer released revision because T_R moved. |
| `member-added` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge the branch has no native edge on. Enters automatically. |
| `member-removed` | informational | — | The candidate removes an edge the branch never claimed or replaced. Applies automatically. |
| `claim-retained` | informational | — | The branch's claim still differs from upstream; the branch wins and upstream is suppressed. `retargeted` distinguishes a suppressed **field value** from a suppressed **re-target**. |
| `claim-superseded` | informational | — | The branch's claim now *matches* what the candidate would natively produce. |
| `claim-orphaned` | **required** | `convert-to-native`, `remove` | The candidate removes an edge the branch **claimed or replaced**. **Blocks the commit.** |
| `member-add-collision` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge whose correlation key coincides with a branch-**native** edge, and the two **differ**. The branch's content wins automatically and is left untouched. |
| `member-add-converged` | informational | — | The same collision, except the candidate's quantity, find number **and** resolved child revision are all identical to the branch's own. The commit retires the branch's now-redundant local edge (`action: "retired"`); the position becomes ordinary `base` content. |

`member-add-collision` and `member-add-converged` are the same coincidence resolving two
ways. Converged requires all three of quantity, find number and resolved child revision to
match; any difference makes it a plain collision. Neither is ever a decision: on a
collision nothing is written and the branch's row stands, and on a converged entry the
commit retires the branch's local edge. A `claim-superseded` claim is never retired.

*The three `claim-*` kinds were `override-retained` / `override-superseded` /
`override-orphaned` before MVP-30309.*

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Two changes to the table:
>
> - **`claim-retained` with `retargeted: true`** offers
>   `availableActions: [accept-source-revision]`. This is an **optional** decision: the
>   `decision` stays `informational`, and a commit without it still succeeds, with the pin
>   winning as today. Accepting pins the row to the candidate's revision and keeps its
>   quantity and find number.
> - **`claim-retained` and `claim-superseded`** carry `revisionAdvances`, which is true when
>   a **tracking** claim's rendered revision moves with this pull. No new entry kind is
>   added, so each position still has exactly one entry. `member-version-advance` still
>   means base content only.
>
> [assumes A-30378-3, A-30378-4, A-30378-10]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Per-field decisions on three kinds, all
> **optional**. `decision` stays `informational`, and a preview with hundreds of entries
> and no `claim-orphaned` still commits with zero decisions.
>
> A field **diverges** when the value the branch holds differs from the candidate's. A
> tracking claim holds no revision, so its revision never diverges, even when `current`
> and `candidate` render different revisions.
>
> | kind | availableActions |
> |---|---|
> | `claim-retained` | `accept-fields`, over the fields that actually diverge. The revision diverges only on a *pinned* claim, exactly when `retargeted`. `accept-source-revision` is also offered when retargeted. |
> | `member-add-collision` | `accept-fields`, over the differing quantity, find number or revision |
> | `claim-superseded` | `release` |
>
> A pull has exactly one **required** kind, `claim-orphaned`, permanently. The other five
> kinds are unchanged. `diffFingerprint`'s mechanism is unchanged, but it digests each
> entry's `availableActions`, so its value changes with the actions offered: a preview
> taken before this ships does not match a commit made after it, and answers
> `STALE_REVISION`.
> [assumes A-30379-3, A-30379-7]

### Why a revision advance is never a decision

A revision is not an independently assertable value. Once you accept that the *line* exists,
which revision it resolves to is a deterministic output of the as-of traversal against T_R —
there is no alternative to offer. The way to hold a revision is to **pin** it — a `claim`
(or `add`, `replace`, `convert-to-native`) carrying a chosen `childItemRevisionId`, a
separate and deliberate act on the delta endpoint. A *tracking* claim holds nothing: it
follows the source's revision and moves with it.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** A `base` row's advance is still never a
> decision. A *pinned* claim that upstream has moved past gets an optional
> `accept-source-revision`: take the candidate's revision, keep everything else. A
> tracking claim's move is flagged with `revisionAdvances` on its `claim-*` entry.
> [assumes A-30378-3, A-30378-4]

### Pins are judged against the tree *after* the pull (MVP-30357)

A row pinned to a revision other than its source line's renders that revision's structure
beneath it, and the source's lines there are suppressed. Which rows that applies to is
decided on the **post-pull** tree, not today's: a pin that upstream moves past becomes one
that suppresses structure, and a pin upstream converges onto, removes or moves stops being
one. Lines hidden behind a post-pull pin get no entry of their own. A branch edit such a pin
will hide is reported instead as a `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` warning — the same warning
the tree read will raise once the commit lands — because the preview is the last point at
which the caller can see that coming.

Pins are judged **per occurrence** (MVP-30214), as the tree renders them. A line behind a
pin on one occurrence that another, unpinned occurrence of the same item still renders is
not hidden: it is reported there like any other line, as `member-added` when it is new.
A hidden-edit warning names every pinned revision that hides the edit.

A pinned claim whose line upstream re-revs is reported as `claim-retained` with
`retargeted: true`: the candidate would resolve the line to a newer revision, and the pin
wins. The commit leaves the pin in place.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Unless the commit carries an
> `accept-source-revision` decision for it. Then the pin moves to the candidate's
> revision, equals the post-pull source line's, and stops rendering a pinned structure,
> so edits it hid render again. The next pull that moves the line reports
> `retargeted: true` again. [assumes A-30378-3]

### Why upstream re-pointing an edge at a *different item* is two entries

The correlation key includes the child item, so it never correlates as one matched pair. It
decomposes into an independent `member-removed` (or `claim-orphaned`) and an independent
`member-added`. `retargeted: true` therefore means a different child **revision**, not a
different child item.

## Truncation

`entriesLimit` caps how many **informational** entries come back. **`required` entries are
never truncated** — they block the commit, so hiding one would silently conceal a blocker.
`summary` always reports the *untruncated* totals, and `diffFingerprint` always covers the
complete diff, so a truncated response is still safe to commit from.

This call is pure and deterministic, so retrieving more needs no cursor: re-issue with a
larger `entriesLimit` and get back a longer, stable prefix of the same diff.

## Access

**Gated on write, not read.** A read-only user is rejected before a pull is even previewed —
the same `Branch_Source__c` update grant `pull` itself requires.

post.summary: Commit a previewed pull, advancing T_R
post.description:
Accepts a newer eBOM root revision into the branch: appends a new `Branch_Source_Rev__c`
advancing T_R, advances the source's root pointer, applies the caller's `claim-orphaned`
dispositions, and retires any `member-add-converged` local edge — **all under one savepoint**.

Returns **`201 Created`**, not 200: a new acceptance record genuinely exists.

## The diff is never trusted from the client

This endpoint **re-resolves the same diff server-side**, through the same code path the
preview used, and answers `STALE_REVISION` the moment the re-resolved `diffFingerprint`
disagrees with what you echoed back, or an `entryId` in `decisions[]` no longer names an
entry in it. Re-preview and resubmit.

A useful side effect: every preview-time failure mode (`NOT_RELEASED`,
`CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH`, `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, `NOT_FOUND`) applies here
for free — nothing in the commit path re-implements them.

## Decisions

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A `claim-orphaned` entry with **no** decision | `409 DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` — the whole commit is rejected. There is no default-accept tier. |
| A decision naming any **other** kind | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` — no other kind is ever actionable. |
| An unrecognised `action` | `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. |
| A `convert-to-native` decision with neither or both of `childItemRevisionId` / `trackChildRevision: true` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` — the whole commit is rejected before any delta or acceptance is written. Both fields are ignored on `remove`. |

| action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `convert-to-native` | Severs the provenance link, keeping the branch-owned quantity and find number, which then resolve on the **branch** clock. **Requires exactly one of** `childItemRevisionId` (stamped onto the native row — send the entry's own `current.detail.childItemRevisionId` to keep what it shows) and `trackChildRevision: true` (float at the read clock); neither or both is `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`, checked with the other decision checks before anything is written. Runs through the ordinary `convert-to-native` delta operation — every invariant that batch enforces applies unchanged, including `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`. |
| `remove` | Appends an **exclude** delta (a deletion marker). **Nothing is hard-deleted.** |

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** An optional decision on a
> `claim-retained` entry with `retargeted: true`:
>
> | action | Effect |
> |---|---|
> | `accept-source-revision` | Pins the claim to the **candidate's** child revision (`candidate.detail.childItemRevisionId`) through a `set-revision` operation, and keeps the branch's quantity and find number. It never becomes an `update`, which cannot change a revision. The row stays pinned. Its pin now equals the post-pull source line's revision, so no pinned structure renders beneath it. The next pull that moves the line reports `retargeted: true` again. `childItemRevisionId` / `trackChildRevision` are ignored on this decision. |
>
> These change in the Decisions table above:
>
> - "A decision naming any other kind → 400" becomes "a decision whose action the entry does
>   not offer in `availableActions` → `400 INVALID_REQUEST`".
> - A `claim-retained` with no decision still commits: it is optional, and only
>   `claim-orphaned` blocks.
>
> The `convert-to-native` revision-choice check is unchanged.
> [assumes A-30378-3, A-30378-10, A-30378-11]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Two more optional actions:
>
> | action | On | Effect |
> |---|---|---|
> | `accept-fields` | `claim-retained`, `member-add-collision` | Takes the fields named in `acceptedFields` (`candidate` or `release` per field), and keeps every other field's branch value. It compiles to **one** delta operation for the row: `update` for quantity / find number alone, and `set-revision` whenever the revision is accepted, carrying any accepted quantity or find number with it. |
> | `release` | `claim-superseded` | On a pinned claim, clears the revision. On a tracking claim, `revert`s the claim so the row becomes `base`. |
>
> The commit refuses with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, and writes nothing, when:
>
> - a field does not diverge, a field name is unknown, or `release` is sent on quantity or
>   find number
> - `acceptedFields` is sent on `claim-orphaned` or with any action but `accept-fields`
> - the decisions would compile to **more than 200 operations**. This is refused whole,
>   never chunked, because a pull commit is atomic.
>
> [assumes A-30379-1, A-30379-2, A-30379-3, A-30379-4, A-30379-5, A-30379-7]

## Claim reconciliation: reported, never persisted

For every existing claimed/replaced field, the commit compares the claim's current value
against what the candidate traversal would natively produce:

- **Differs** → reported as `claim-retained` / **reaffirmed**. It stays active and
  continues to govern future pulls. **Nothing new is persisted** — the comparison is
  reconstructed from the accepted source version on every pull, so a "reaffirmation" record
  would change no rendered value.
- **Matches** → reported as `claim-superseded`. Also **never deleted and never written**.
  Retiring it would mean a branch that once happened to agree with upstream would silently
  start accepting upstream changes from then on.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Nothing is persisted *unless the caller
> decided*. An `accept-source-revision` decision writes one new payload revision for its
> row. [assumes A-30378-3]

`Edge_Key__c` and `Alias__c` are likewise **never re-stamped**. They keep meaning "the
upstream line this edge was originally minted against", independent of the correlation key a
pull actually joins on.

## Retiring a converged local add

A `member-add-converged` entry is retired without a decision. "Retired" means **one appended
`Branch_Member__c` row of `Delta_Type__c = 'Revert'`**, with `Claims_Source__c` null —
nothing is deleted, and a read dated before this commit still renders the local add. The
position becomes ordinary `base` content resolved at the new T_R, so it follows the source
from then on.

Reported in `applied[]` as `{"kind": "member-add-converged", "action": "retired"}`, inside
the same savepoint as the rest of the commit.

## Atomicity

One outer savepoint around both the disposition batch and the acceptance insert, rolled back
on any exception from either. A failure part way leaves the prior accepted revision and T_R
in place, with no orphaned claim, exclude or claim-status records.

## The already-current commit

A commit submitted when the candidate equals the currently-accepted root **still succeeds**:
it appends a new acceptance (advancing `Accepted_At__c` with the same `Source_TimePoint__c`)
and returns `applied: []`. Same reading the preview takes of the read side.

## What a pull leaves alone

Branch-**native** content is unaffected, with one exception: the `member-add-converged`
retirement above. A local add that still differs from the source (`member-add-collision`) is
left untouched, as is native content the source never collided with.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Branch_Source_Rev__c`, `Branch_Member__c`, `CI__c`, `CI_Rev__c`,
`Assembly_CI__c` and `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`, **and edit** on `Branch_Source__c`,
`Assembly_CI__c` and `CI_Rev__c`. Both gates run **before the body is read**.

get.summary: Compare a branch against another configuration
get.description:
The structural difference between two configurations: which members each holds, and where
the two disagree on quantity, find number or the child revision they resolve to.

The **left** side is the branch the path names. The **right** side is named by
`rightKind` + `rightId`, and may be another branch, a baseline, a source, or a released
eBOM revision — so one endpoint answers eBOM-against-MBOM, MBOM-against-MBOM and
MBOM-against-its-own-baseline rather than three.

**This call is pure.** No DML anywhere behind it. Two calls with the same inputs against an
unchanged org return identical entries, `entryId` values included. Only the read clock moves:
`generatedAt`, each side's `asOf` when the caller sent none, and the `governingTimestamp` of
every state that answers to `asOf`.

## The right-hand side

| `rightKind` | `rightId` names | Resolves to | Its clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | `Branch__c` | the branch's own effective structure, deltas overlaid | `rightAsOf`, defaulting to now |
| `baseline` | `Baseline__c` | the branch re-resolved at the boundary the cut recorded | the baseline's frozen `Resolution_TimePoint__c`; `rightAsOf` is **refused** |
| `source` | `Branch_Source__c` | what that source *supplies*, with no branch deltas folded in | the acceptance in effect at `rightAsOf` |
| `ebom` | `Item_Revision__c` | a raw eBOM walk beneath that revision, no branch in the picture | `rightAsOf`, defaulting to **that revision's release date** |

`rightKind` is matched **case-insensitively** — `rightKind=Branch` is a 200. The values
are published lower-case and that is the spelling to send; normalising a published wire
value is a courtesy the HTTP surface affords, and the service behind it stays
case-sensitive.

A `source` with nothing accepted yet resolves to no root and no members. That is a `200`,
not an error: every member of the other side lands as added or removed.

## Entry kinds

| kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root-version-differs` | The two sides resolve **different root revisions**. One entry per comparison, never one per edge. |
| `member-added` | The correlation key is present on the **right** and absent on the left. |
| `member-removed` | The correlation key is present on the **left** and absent on the right. |
| `member-differs` | Present on both, content disagrees. `differingFields[]` names which of `quantity` / `findNumber` / `childRevision`. |
| `member-unchanged` | Present on both and identical. **Emitted only when `includeUnchanged=true`.** |

One entry per correlation key, always — which is why `member-differs` carries a list rather
than splitting into three kinds. `entryId` hashes `(kind, parent item, child item,
secondary unique key)`, so two entries on one key would collide.

`root-version-differs` fires whenever the two **resolved root revisions** differ, and that
includes the case where the two roots are different *items* — a different item's revision
is trivially a different revision. That is what stops `identical` reporting two unrelated
assemblies as the same configuration. The abnormal shape is named separately, by the
`COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER` warning.

### The correlation key is the pull's key

`(Parent_Item__c, Item__c, Secondary_Unique_Key__c)` — the same join
[pull-preview](#operation/previewMbomPull) documents in full, for the same reason: the
parent *item* does not move when its revision does, so the key survives the BOM clone a
revision advance performs. Edges at one key are told apart and paired exactly as on the
pull: by parent revision within a side, so a side that renders one parent item at two
revisions compares cleanly. A `replace` substitute that stands aside is a one-sided
member. Where the join cannot tell which member corresponds to which, the answer is
`AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` (422) rather than a guess.

### Exclusion tombstones are filtered out before the join

Both sides are reduced to what the configuration *contains* — the same
`isContainedMember` predicate a baseline read applies — so a tombstone never becomes a
member. A member excluded on the left therefore surfaces as **`member-added`** against a
right that still supplies it: the left does not contain it and the right does, which is the
honest answer for a symmetric compare and what keeps branch-against-baseline
self-consistent, since a baseline's rows were filtered by that same predicate when it was
cut.

### Provenance is reported, never classified

Each entry's `left` / `right` state carries `provenance` and `governingClock`, so a
claiming-versus-base difference is visible without a kind of its own. A provenance-only
difference is **not** a content difference and produces no entry: the same part at the same
quantity in the same position is the same member however each side came to hold it. A
branch that claimed a member without changing it therefore reads as unchanged against its
own source.

## What a comparison deliberately does not have

- **No decision tier and no actions.** A comparison initiates nothing, so `decision`,
  `availableActions`, `retargeted` and `claimKind` are **absent** from an entry rather
  than defaulted — a consumer cannot read a default as an answer. That is also why
  `CompareEntry` is not the pull's `DiffEntry`, whose `current` / `candidate` naming would
  be a lie on a symmetric pair.
- **No `diffFingerprint`.** The pull carries one so a commit can fail fast on a stale
  preview. There is no commit here, so a digest would be a field nobody could act on.

## `summary`, and the one thing that is easy to get wrong

`total` and `byKind` count the entries **emitted**, so both move with `includeUnchanged`.
`added`, `removed`, `differing` and **`unchanged` do not** — `unchanged` is derived from the
matched correlation keys and is therefore **populated whether or not the unchanged rows were
asked for**. That is the point of it: the default response emits no row for an identical
member, and a caller still needs to know how much of the configuration matched without
paying for the rows. So `summary.unchanged` does **not** always equal
`byKind['member-unchanged']`; with `includeUnchanged=false` the latter is `0`.

`byKind` is **pre-seeded with all five kinds at zero**, unlike the pull's summary, which
carries only the kinds it observed. A comparison is read by a client rendering a fixed set
of counters, and an absent key would make every one of them a null check.

Counts are always over the **untruncated** comparison.

## Ordering and truncation

Entries are ordered by **breadcrumb path, then find number, then child item id, then kind**,
with `entryId` last purely as a total-order guarantee. A deliberate divergence from the
pull's `entryId`-hash order: a pull preview is read as a flat decision list, while a
comparison is read against a tree, and hash order scatters siblings.

`entriesLimit` caps `entries` as a **plain prefix** — unlike the pull, a comparison has no
`required` tier that trimming could silently hide. `summary` is left alone, which is what
makes `truncated: true` actionable rather than merely true; re-issue with a larger limit to
get a longer, stable prefix of the same comparison.

The default cap is **not** raised by `includeUnchanged=true`, deliberately: a 500-edge BOM
truncates at 200 and says so, rather than silently returning a response an order of
magnitude larger than the caller expected.

> Truncation is applied by the REST layer. The service beneath it always returns a complete
> comparison, so a Flow or an LWC controller calling it directly sees every entry with
> `truncated: false` and `entriesLimit: null`. Over HTTP both fields are always filled in.

## Access

**Gated on read, not write** — deliberately unlike
[pull-preview](#operation/previewMbomPull), which requires the same write grant the commit
does because previewing a pull is initiating one. A comparison initiates nothing, and
refusing a read-only user the ability to *look* at a difference has no justification.
Confirmed with the PM: read-only users may compare. This is not a copied-and-forgotten gate.

Each side is gated on the object it is addressed by: `Branch__c` for a branch,
`Baseline__c` **and** `Branch__c` for a baseline, `Branch_Source__c` for a source,
`Item_Revision__c` for an eBOM revision.

right side, which resolves at its own recorded timepoint and could not honour a
different one.

`ASOF_INVALID` / `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — either clock could not be parsed, or names a moment
that has not happened.

An unrecognised `includeUnchanged` is **not** an error — see that parameter.

`NOT_FOUND` — the path id names no branch or names another object; `rightId` names
