get.summary: Compare a baseline against another configuration
get.description:
The same comparison as [`compareBranch`](#operation/compareBranch) — same right-hand types,
same kinds, same summary, same truncation — with a **baseline** on the left instead of a
branch.

It exists because a baseline has to be able to sit on the left as well as the right: "what
has this branch done since we froze it?" and "what changed between these two builds?" are
both baseline-rooted questions, and neither can be asked by naming the baseline on the right
alone.

## `asOf` is refused here, not ignored

The left side is a baseline, so it resolves at the boundary its cut recorded. A second
clock has nothing to answer, and accepting one would let a caller believe they had asked a
temporal question and been given a temporal answer. Sending `asOf` is a
`400 INVALID_REQUEST` — the same reading
[`getBaselineTree`](#operation/getBaselineTree) takes. `rightAsOf` is still accepted,
unless the *right* side is a baseline too.

There is deliberately **no** `sources/{id}/comparison` and no eBOM-rooted left side. Both
can still be compared — as the right-hand side of a branch or baseline — and eBOM against
eBOM is already served by Propel's existing BOM Compare, which a third surface would
duplicate.

## Access

Read, not write, exactly as the branch-rooted endpoint. A baseline side is gated on
`Baseline__c` **and** `Branch__c`, because reading one resolves the branch behind it.

200.description: The comparison, in the shape `compareBranch` returns — `left.kind` is `baseline`.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — everything `compareBranch` refuses, **plus `asOf`**, which a
baseline left side cannot honour.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (asOf cannot be supplied for a baseline: a baseline resolves at its own recorded timepoint, and honouring a different one would not be that baseline)

404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — the path id names no baseline, `rightId` names nothing or the wrong object, or the path carries a trailing segment.

sessionToken.description:
Standard Salesforce OAuth 2.0 access token or session id, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

BranchId.name: branchId
BranchId.description:
Id of the `Branch__c`. Returned as `branchId` from `POST /mbom/mboms`.

A malformed id, or a well-formed id of the wrong object, is a **404** — not a 500 and not a
403. The URI is what names the resource, so a path naming nothing is a path to nothing, and
the two tree endpoints therefore cannot be confused for each other by a caller that swaps a
branch id for a source id.

SourceId.name: sourceId
SourceId.description:
Id of the `Branch_Source__c`. Returned as **`sourceId`** from `POST /mbom/mboms`.

In Phase 1 a branch has exactly one source, of `Source_Type__c = 'Ebom'`. The owning branch is
reached through `Branch_Source__c.Downstream_Branch__c`, which is why there is no separate
`branchId` segment on these paths.

BaselineId.name: baselineId
BaselineId.description: Id of the `Baseline__c`, returned from the cut.

AsOf.name: asOf
AsOf.description:
The **branch** clock for this read. Defaults to the server clock when omitted; a future value
is `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` (400).

Governs the branch's own deltas, local content and substitutes. It does **not** govern
`base` content, which always resolves at T_R — that is the two-clock model, and passing
`asOf` to the source traversal is the single change that would quietly make a pinned MBOM
float.

Accepts ISO-8601 (`2026-02-01T00:00:00Z`, `2026-02-01T00:00:00+05:30`) and the
space-separated Apex form (`2026-02-01 03:04:05`, interpreted as GMT). A `+` offset is
repaired server-side after query-string decoding turns it into a space, so a legal ISO offset
does not fail in transport.

Flat.name: flat
Flat.description:
Response shape. **Flat is the default, and only an explicit `flat=false` nests.**

Anything unrecognised (`flat=0`, `flat=no`) falls back to flat rather than raising — partly
because `Boolean.valueOf('0')` is `false` and the obvious implementation would *nest* for
`flat=0`, the opposite of what that caller asked for, and partly because a flat response
carries `parentItemId` on every row and is therefore losslessly re-nestable by the client.

Not accepted by `GET /mbom/sources/{sourceId}/tree` — silently ignored there, so one
parameter set can be sent to both tree reads.

EntriesLimit.name: entriesLimit
EntriesLimit.description:
Caps how many **`informational`** entries the preview returns. `required` entries are always
returned in full regardless of this cap.

Must be a positive integer; anything else is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` rather than a silent
fallback to the default.

RightKind.name: rightKind
RightKind.description:
What the **right-hand** side of the comparison is. Required — a comparison against nothing
in particular is half a request, so a missing or unrecognised value is
`400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

- `branch` — another `Branch__c`, resolved with its own deltas overlaid.
- `baseline` — a `Baseline__c`, replayed at the boundary its cut recorded.
- `source` — a `Branch_Source__c`: what that source *supplies*, with no branch deltas
  folded in. This is the "what have I changed relative to upstream?" comparison.
- `ebom` — a released `Item_Revision__c`, walked raw, with no branch in the picture.

**Matched case-insensitively**, so `Branch` and `BRANCH` are both accepted. Send the
lower-case spelling: that is the published value, and it is what comes back in
`right.kind`.

RightId.name: rightId
RightId.description:
The record the right-hand side is. Its object must match `rightKind` —
`Branch__c`, `Baseline__c`, `Branch_Source__c` or `Item_Revision__c` respectively.

**Absent is a 400** (the caller described half a comparison); **present but naming nothing,
or naming another object, is a 404** (the caller named a resource that is not there). The
same split the path ids make.

RightAsOf.name: rightAsOf
RightAsOf.description:
The **right** side's read clock. `asOf` governs the left side; each side keeps its own pair
of clocks and never borrows the other's, which is why there are two parameters rather than
one. A branch read at now against a baseline frozen in March is two configurations at two
instants, and both are published on the response.

Defaults differ by side type — now for `branch` and `source`, and for `ebom` **that
revision's own release date**, since a raw eBOM walk has no acceptance to pin it and "the
eBOM of revision X" honestly means the eBOM as it stood when X was released.

**Refused for a `baseline` right side** (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`), which resolves at the
timepoint its cut recorded. Parsing and the future-value rule are `asOf`'s, unchanged.

IncludeUnchanged.name: includeUnchanged
IncludeUnchanged.description:
Emit a `member-unchanged` entry for every correlation key present and identical on both
sides, turning the response into the **complete merged BOM** — one entry per key across
both sides, which is what a side-by-side tree renders from a single call.

Defaults to `false`. **Only an explicit `true` (any case) turns it on**; anything else —
`includeUnchanged=1`, `=yes` — falls back to the default rather than raising, because the
fallback is the smaller response and loses no information: `summary.unchanged` carries the
count either way.

It costs no extra query. It does **not** raise `entriesLimit`, and it moves `summary.total`
and `summary.byKind`, which count entries emitted — see the endpoint description.

Provenance.description:
Where a rendered row comes from. **Derived at read time, never stored** — `claiming` and
`new` differ by exactly one field on the winning delta row (`Claims_Source__c`).

The taxonomy has two axes — whether a record exists upstream, and whether the branch has
taken it over:

| | exists upstream (*source*) | has a branch CI (*native*) |
|---|---|---|
| untouched | `base` | — |
| taken over | — | `claiming` |
| branch only | — | `new` |

- `base` — supplied by the source; no branch-owned record exists.
- `claiming` — a branch row that takes over a source row (copy-on-write ownership).
- `new` — branch-owned with no upstream counterpart ("native").
- `nested` — a descendant of a locally added or substituted assembly, rendered from that
  item's own eBOM; or, since MVP-30357, a descendant of a **pinned** row whose chosen
  revision differs from its source line's, rendered from the pinned revision's eBOM in
  place of the source's lines. Read-only: every row in such a subtree carries
  `isEditable: false`, and the pull diff excludes them entirely. Appears on tree rows only,
  never in a diff entry's `MemberState`.

There is no `excluded` value: exclusion is tracked as a separate boolean alongside
provenance, never as a value of it. Nor is there a `claimed` value for a source row some
branch has taken over: that answer is branch-relative, so a source read with no branch
could not give it.

**Renamed in MVP-30309 (breaking).** `inherited` → `base`, `claimed` → `claiming`,
`local` → `new`; `nested` is unchanged.

GoverningClock.description:
Which clock resolves this member. `source` is the pinned T_R (it only advances when a pull is
committed); `branch` is the caller's `asOf`. Both are legitimately in play at once, which is
what makes mixed revisions of one item possible.

CiKind.description:
Discriminator for the configuration-item type, and therefore for the shape of
`MemberState.detail`. `assembly-edge` is the only member type implemented; this enum is the
extension point where a future CI type is added.

`source` appears only on the root-level `source-version-advance` entry's `target` (and on the
root segment of every `path[]`), because that entry is about the source's root **item**
rather than an edge beneath it: it has no parent, no quantity and no find number.

rootItemRevisionId.description:
The **released** `Item_Revision__c` the MBOM is built over. Its `Released_Date_Time__c`
becomes T_R.

mbomName.description:
`MBOM__c.Name`. Required, and a blank value is refused with `INVALID_REQUEST` rather than
being left to DML — a custom object's Text `Name` is unenforced by the API, so a blank
one would silently produce an MBOM named after its own record id that nobody can search
for.

branchLabel.description:
Lands on **both** `Branch__c.Name` (what every Salesforce list view and lookup shows) and
`Branch__c.Label__c`. Bounded by the shorter of the two fields.

branchId.description: The initial `Branch__c`. Use it on every `/branches/...` endpoint.

sourceId.description:
The `Branch_Source__c` linking the branch to its eBOM. **This is the `sourceId`** on
every `/sources/...` endpoint.

sourceRevisionId.description: The first acceptance, carrying T_R in `Source_TimePoint__c`.

StructureTree.description: The response body of **both** tree reads — a branch's effective structure, and a source's structure on its own.

asOf.description: The timepoint this tree was resolved at, echoed so the response is self-describing. Present even when the caller sent none.

rootRevisionId.description: The root `Item_Revision__c` the structure hangs from.

sourceTimePoint.description: **T_R** — the source timepoint `base` rows resolve at.

rows.description: Always present; empty rather than absent.

warnings.description: Always present; empty rather than absent.

TreeRow.description:
One row of a resolved tree. The same shape serves both response shapes: in the **nested**
shape `childRows` holds the subtree and `parentItemId` is still populated; in the **flat**
shape every row is a sibling and `childRows` is empty — so a client can rebuild the tree from
a flat response without a second request. The one exception is an item rendered at two
revisions, whose occurrences' children all name the same `parentItemId`; see the branch
tree read's "Flat vs. nested".

edgeId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` edge. **Null for a `base` row** that no branch has claimed. Suppressed on baseline rows.

edgeKey.description:
The legacy `Assembly__c` line id, or a synthetic key for branch-local content:
`new-{branchId}-{parentItemId}-{childItemId}` for an `add`, or
`replaces-{branchId}-{supersededEdgeKey}-{newChildItemId}` for a substitute. Suppressed
on baseline rows.

The `add` prefix was `local-` before MVP-30309. Keys minted before the rename keep the
old prefix — an edge key is identity and is never re-stamped — so treat the key as
opaque and never parse the prefix.

A substitute always carries its own `replaces-…` key, even when its child item already
has its own line under the same parent: the two render as two rows, each under its own
key (see the branch tree read).

governingTimestamp.description:
T_R for a `base` row; `asOf` for every other row — `claiming`, `new` and `nested`.

A `claiming` row answers to `asOf` because this one field also governs the branch's own
quantity and find number, so it does not always name the clock that chose the row's
child revision (see `AssemblyEdgeDetail.childItemRevisionId`).

**On a baseline row it is collapsed, not suppressed:** every row carries the baseline's
own `resolutionTimePoint`. A frozen record honours exactly one timepoint, so a per-row
clock there would imply the reader could re-resolve at it — but the value is stated
rather than nulled, so one client code path renders baseline and tree rows alike.

sourceId.description: The `Branch_Source__c` this row came from. Null for a branch-local row.

isExcluded.description:
True for a tombstoned row. **Rendered by the branch tree read** so the editor can see
what was removed; **filtered out** by the baseline read.

isReplaced.description: True when this row stands in for another (`replace`). Populated on baseline rows too — a null would render a substituted part identically to an ordinary one.

isEditable.description:
False on any row inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly, or of a
row pinned to a revision other than its source line's (MVP-30357). Every delta op
refuses those rows with `NOT_EDITABLE`, so a UI offering an action on one is offering an
action the API will reject.

isCollapsedCollision.description:
True when one BOM position is asserted by both the branch and its source and the two
render as a single row, with the branch's content winning. A tree read carries a
`MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` warning alongside it.

Defaults to `false`. Populated on baseline rows too, where — because a baseline
forwards drift warnings only — it is the sole signal of the collapse.

isPinned.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** True when this row stores a child
revision somebody **chose**: an `add` or `replace` that sent `childItemRevisionId`, a
`claim` that pinned, or a `convert-to-native` that stamped. Never null.

It follows the explicit choice only, never what the row happens to render:

- A tracking claim or a floating row is `false`, even when it resolves to exactly the
  revision a pin would have named.
- A pin **equal** to its source line's revision is `true`, although it renders no
  pinned structure.
- A floating `new` row that renders a pinned structure because the read clock moved
  past T_R is `false`: nobody chose it.
- Tombstones, `nested` rows and every row of a source tree are `false`.

The structural sense of "pinned" is a different signal: a row whose revision differs
from its source line's renders that revision's structure and can raise
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`. Never derive one from the other. Populated on baseline
rows too.

wasClaimed.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** True on a `new` row that once claimed
a source row, and that `convert-to-native` flipped from `claiming` to `new`. The
provenance says the row is the branch's own now. This says it did not start that way,
which an audit of a released configuration needs to see. Never null.

A display fact about one row's history, deliberately **not** a provenance value.
Populated on baseline rows too, resolved at the baseline's own timepoint. Since
MVP-30357 every convert makes a stamp-or-track choice, so a `wasClaimed` row may or may
not be `isPinned`.

pinnedById.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** On a **baseline** row with
`isPinned: true`, the user who created the payload revision carrying the row's current
value. Null on every live tree read, and on every unpinned row.

It names who last revised the row, not necessarily who first chose the revision: an
`update` that changed only the quantity carries the pin forward and becomes the author.
A live read is left null because its winning revision can still move.

pinnedAt.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** When that payload revision was
created. Null exactly where `pinnedById` is.

childRows.description: Populated in the nested shape only; **empty, never null**, in the flat shape.

TreeWarning.description:
A condition worth telling the user about that does **not** block the read. Shared by the tree
reads, the baseline read and the pull preview.

The key is **`warningCode`**, matching the existing mBOM convention — never `code`, which
this API reserves for the error body.

warningCode.description:
The complete vocabulary.

| Value | Status |
|---|---|
| `MIXED_REVISION` | ✅ shipped |
| `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` | ✅ shipped |
| `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` | ✅ shipped |
| `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED` | ✅ shipped |
| `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` | ✅ shipped |
| `MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` | ✅ shipped |
| `COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER` | ✅ shipped |
| `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` | 🚧 MVP-30375 |
| `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` | 🚧 MVP-30376 |

- `MIXED_REVISION` — one item rendered at more than one revision in the same tree,
  because two clocks are in play. Legal and expected; warned, never blocked. Each
  occurrence renders its own revision's structure.
- `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different **row count** than its cut
  recorded.
- `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different number of **`claiming`**
  rows than its cut recorded. Separate from the count drift because severing a claim
  moves no row: the same rows come back, one of them no longer a claim. Narrow —
  only reachable when the severing delta lands in the same whole second as the cut,
  since a saved `Datetime` has second precision.
- `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED` — the structure of a locally added or substituted assembly, or
  of a pinned revision, was dropped because walking it reached a cycle. The rest of the
  tree is still returned; when pins were involved it falls back to the unsuppressed
  source structure, and raises no `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`.
- `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` (MVP-30357) — some of the branch's edits take no effect,
  because a pinned row's own revision structure replaced the source lines they sit on:
  a claim, exclusion, update or substitute on a suppressed line (and on no line still
  rendered elsewhere), or an `add` under an item only the suppressed structure
  supplied. Rendered, never refused. Raised on the tree reads and on the pull preview,
  where it describes the tree **after** the commit. A revision cannot be changed in place
  this release, so the remedy is to `revert` the pinned claim and claim the line again —
  tracking, or pinned to the source line's own revision — in a later request.
  **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** The remedy becomes `set-revision` on
  the pinned row. Clear it with `trackChildRevision: true`, or pin it to the source
  line's own revision. Either keeps the row's quantity and find number, and the hidden
  edits render again. [assumes A-30378-2]
- `MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` — one BOM position was asserted by **both** the branch and its
  source, and the branch's content won. The two rows render as one, carrying
  `isCollapsedCollision: true`. Not raised once a pull has retired a *converged* local
  add, because only the source asserts the position from then on.
- `COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER` — a comparison's two sides are rooted at different **items**,
  so they have no members in common and every entry is an addition or a removal for
  that reason alone. The comparison still answers; refusing would be the wrong call for
  a read. Comparison responses only, where it is reported on **`leftWarnings`** — it is
  about the pair rather than either side, the response has two warning lists and no
  third, and the left is the side the caller addressed by path. It carries no `itemId`
  and no revisions: there is no single item it is about, and `left` / `right` already
  publish both roots.
- `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** A baseline
  re-derived a different number of **explicitly pinned** rows (`isPinned`) than its cut
  recorded. The count covers contained members, excluding tombstones, `nested` rows and
  edits hidden behind a pin. It catches a revision decision moving where no row count
  or claim count moved. Baseline reads only. It carries no `itemId` and empty arrays,
  like the other drift codes. A baseline cut before the ticket has no count and never
  raises it. [assumes A-30375-5]
- `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** A row
  holds a chosen child revision that has since been **Cancelled or Expired**. The row
  still renders that revision: nothing is substituted, and the read does not fail.
  Nobody chose a replacement, and a read must not break because a revision was
  cancelled elsewhere in the org.

  One warning per row, not deduplicated by item. `itemId` is the row's child item and
  `itemRevisionIds` is the stored revision. It is never raised by a row that stores no
  revision: a tracking claim or a floating row already resolves through a query that
  skips dead revisions. It is not raised by a tombstone, or by an edit hidden behind a
  pin. On a dead pin with nested structure, it names the pinned row, not the rows
  beneath it. Branch tree read only. [assumes A-30376-1, A-30376-2, A-30376-3]

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label. Translated; never parse it.

itemId.description:
Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the item rendered at more than one revision — on
`MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION`, naming the child item whose position collapsed, and on
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`, naming the child item of the edited line a pinned
revision's structure replaced (or, on a pull preview, will replace).
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** Also on `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`,
naming the child item of the row holding the dead revision. [assumes A-30376-3]

itemRevisionIds.description:
Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the revisions in play — and on
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`, where it lists the pinned revisions whose structure hid
the edit (each is the `detail.childItemRevisionId` of a pinned row), with
`governingTimestamps` left empty. Every other code leaves it empty.
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** Also on `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`,
where it holds exactly one id, the Cancelled or Expired stored revision, with
`governingTimestamps` left empty. [assumes A-30376-3]

governingTimestamps.description: Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the clock that governed each, positionally aligned with `itemRevisionIds`.

atomic.description:
All-or-nothing when true. **A null is treated as `true`** — the safer contract wins the
default, so a caller who did not think about the failure mode gets all-or-nothing rather
than a half-applied branch.

asOf.description:
Resolves the branch **once** for the whole batch; every operation then validates against
that one snapshot, so a batch cannot see the tree shift underneath it halfway through.

Defaults to the server clock; never accepted in the future. A **past** value means
"validate against the configuration as it stood then" — it never dates the write. Several
operations refuse a past value outright; see the endpoint description.

operations.description: At most 200 — beyond that, `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before anything is resolved.

DeltaOperation.description:
One operation. The shape is a **union across all eight operations** rather than a class per
operation, because the batch arrives as one JSON array. `op` selects which fields are
meaningful, and each operation validates its own required fields — an `add` with no
`parentItemId` is that operation's error to raise, not a deserialisation failure.

Unknown keys are **silently ignored** (the deserialiser is lenient), so a *mistyped* field
name reads as a null id. `rootItemRevisionld` with an `l` will answer `NOT_FOUND`, not a
schema error.

op.description:
Matched case-insensitively. An unknown value is a **per-operation** validation failure (`INVALID_REQUEST`), not an exception — one mistyped name in a batch of 200 must not read as a server fault.

| Value | Status |
|---|---|
| `claim`, `update`, `add`, `exclude`, `restore`, `replace`, `revert`, `convert-to-native` | ✅ shipped |
| `set-revision` | 🚧 MVP-30378 — today it answers `INVALID_REQUEST` (unknown op) |

clientRef.description:
Opaque caller token, echoed verbatim on this operation's result. Set it to correlate
results with a UI row; the server never interprets it. Correlating on order alone breaks
the moment anything is reordered, and on `clientRef` alone breaks when you do not set it
— so `index` is stated too.

ebomAssemblyId.description:
The legacy `Assembly__c` line. Used by: `claim`, `exclude`, `update` (the `CLAIM_REQUIRED` path), `revert` (the second-revert path).

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Also `set-revision`, whose `base`-row
answer is `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. [assumes A-30378-1]

assemblyCiId.description:
An existing `Assembly_CI__c` edge to `update`. The ordinary form.

The **request** keeps this name while the result publishes the same id as `edgeId`.
Not an oversight: a request is deserialized into a flat Apex type whose field names
are the wire names, and the operation an id belongs to is known only after `op` is
read — so a request field cannot be enveloped per CI type the way a response can.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Also addresses `set-revision`. For
> `update` and `set-revision` it also finds a row hidden behind a pin, which
> `ebomAssemblyId` never does. [assumes A-30378-1, A-30378-5]

replacedEbomAssemblyId.description: `replace` only — the legacy line being superseded. Must be an eBOM-derived row; a branch-local row cannot be replaced.

newChildItemId.description: `replace` only — the substitute part. Its revision **floats** at the read clock unless `childItemRevisionId` pins it.

quantity.description:
Used by `update`, `add`, `replace`.

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Also optional on `set-revision`.
[assumes A-30379-5]

findNumber.description:
Used by `update`, `add`, `replace`.

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Also optional on `set-revision`.
[assumes A-30379-5]

childItemRevisionId.description:
An explicit child `Item_Revision__c` for the row this operation creates or takes over —
`add`, `replace`, `claim` or `convert-to-native` (MVP-30357). Ignored on every other
operation.

A value means "use exactly this revision, whatever the clock says": a deliberate pin,
never a default. It must be a revision **of the operation's child item** — the claimed
line's child for `claim`, the substitute for `replace`, the converted row's child for
`convert-to-native` — or the operation answers `422 REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH` (also the
answer for an id naming no revision you can see).

- On `add` and `replace`, **blank means track**, and is the default: the row floats at
  the read clock.
- On `claim` and `convert-to-native`, blank is **not a choice on its own**: send either
  this or `trackChildRevision: true` — exactly one — or the operation answers
  `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`.

There is no server-side "pin current". To pin what the tree shows, or to have a convert
keep what it shows, send back that row's `detail.childItemRevisionId`.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** Also read by `update` sent with
> `autoClaim: true`. On a `base` edge it pins the claim the update performs. On an owned
> edge it must equal the stored revision, or the update answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST`
> naming `set-revision`. [assumes A-30377-1]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** It is the payload of `set-revision`:
> the revision to pin, validated against the row's own child item. Clearing is
> `trackChildRevision: true`, not a null here. A plain `update` that sends a non-null
> value is refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming `set-revision`, instead of being
> silently ignored as today. [assumes A-30378-2, A-30378-6]

trackChildRevision.description:
`claim` and `convert-to-native` only: `true` stores **no** revision (MVP-30357). `false`
and null both mean "not chosen".

- On `claim`, the row **follows the source**: it keeps rendering exactly the revision its
  unclaimed self would, at the accepted source's T_R, and moves when a pull accepts a
  newer source. It does not float at the read clock.
- On `convert-to-native`, the row has no source left to follow, so it **floats at the
  read clock**, exactly like an `add`.

Each of the two must carry exactly one of this (`true`) and `childItemRevisionId`;
neither, or both, is `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`. **Ignored, not refused, on every
other operation** — `add` and `replace` already track when `childItemRevisionId` is
blank, and refusing it would make one shared client payload shape invalid for them.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** It is also read by `update` sent with
> `autoClaim: true`, which makes the same exactly-one choice. See `autoClaim`.
> [assumes A-30377-1]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** On `set-revision`, `true` **clears**
> the stored revision, with the same exactly-one rule. A cleared claim follows its
> source line at T_R. A cleared `new` row or substitute floats at the read clock.
> [assumes A-30378-2]

autoClaim.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** `update` only. When `true`, an update
of a `base` edge **claims it and revises it in one operation**, instead of answering
`409 CLAIM_REQUIRED`. Today that needs two requests, because a batch validates every
operation against one pre-batch snapshot.

- **The implicit claim makes the same revision choice `claim` does.** Whenever
  `autoClaim` is `true`, send exactly one of `trackChildRevision: true` or
  `childItemRevisionId`. `trackChildRevision: true` is the expected case: the row keeps
  following its source line. `childItemRevisionId` claims and pins. Neither, or both,
  answers `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`, whatever state the row is in, and nothing is
  claimed. There is no default, for the reason `claim` has none.
- **The result reports the claim.** `DeltaResult.claimed` is `true`. `CLAIM_REQUIRED`
  would have disclosed the eBOM line before the fact; this discloses it after.
- **On an edge the branch already owns**, the flag is a no-op claim, and the update
  proceeds normally with `claimed` left null. `trackChildRevision` is ignored there. A
  `childItemRevisionId` equal to the stored one is accepted. A **different** one is
  refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming `set-revision`, rather than being silently
  dropped.
- **It bypasses no other guard.** These all still refuse the operation:
  - `NOT_EDITABLE` on a nested row, `NOT_SUPPLIED` on an excluded one, `STALE_REVISION`
  - a non-positive quantity, or a second operation on the same edge in the batch
  - every guard `claim` applies: a past `asOf` on a `base` edge (`INVALID_REQUEST`),
    `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`, and a membership change on the same row earlier in the
    batch. So `[replace(L, X), update(L, autoClaim)]` is refused, as
    `[replace(L, X), claim(L)]` is.
  - On an edge the branch already owns, no claim happens, so a past `asOf` stays
    tolerated as on plain `update`.
- A row hidden behind a pin, addressed by `ebomAssemblyId`, answers `NOT_FOUND`, as
  plain `update` does today. `autoClaim` does not change how a row is found; reaching
  one by `assemblyCiId` is MVP-30378's concern (A-30378-5).

`false` and null both mean off: today's `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, still carrying the eBOM line.
Ignored, not refused, on every other operation. [assumes A-30377-1, A-30377-4,
A-30377-5]

atomic.description: Echoed, so the response says which contract it was written under.

asOf.description:
The timepoint the whole batch resolved against. It matters more here than on a read — the
caller may have sent none at all, and this is the only way to learn which server clock
the batch actually used.

applied.description: Count of operations that succeeded. Stated so a client can act on the summary without walking `results`.

results.description: One entry per requested operation, **in request order**, success or failure.

index.description: Zero-based position of this operation in the request.

clientRef.description: Your own token, echoed verbatim. Null when you set none.

errorCode.description:
The error code on failure, null on success. Note the key is **`errorCode`** here, inside
a per-operation result — the top-level *error body* uses `code`.

The values are `RestError.code`'s vocabulary — that enum is the complete list. Left a
plain string here so a code added to the vocabulary never makes a batch result fail
validation in an older client.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label. Never parsed.

ciId.description: The `CI__c` this operation created or acted on.

edgeId.description:
The edge this operation created or acted on, in its CI type's own vocabulary — an
`Assembly_CI__c` for the assembly type. The same value, under the same name, that
`TreeRow.edgeId` publishes. The REQUEST field `assemblyCiId` is a different field
and keeps its name.

forked.description:
True when an `update` had to allocate a **new** `CI_Rev__c` rather than edit one in
place, because a baseline had frozen it. Surfaced because your next read will show a
revision number you did not ask for.

**Deliberately not defaulted.** Only `update` forks. `null` means *not applicable*
(there was nothing to fork on a `claim` or an `exclude`); `false` means *this write could
have forked and did not*. A client must treat them differently, so the field must be able
to say both.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** `null` on an `update` that
> auto-claimed (`claimed: true`). It minted a claim's first revision, exactly as `claim`
> does, so there was nothing to fork. [assumes A-30377-3]

claimed.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30377, not yet implemented.** `true` when this operation took
ownership of a `base` edge on the caller's behalf, which only an `update` sent with
`autoClaim: true` can do. Nothing else in the response would say so: `edgeId` is
populated either way.

**Never `false`.** It is `null` whenever no claim was performed: `autoClaim` off, an
`autoClaim` on an edge the branch already owned, a failure, and every other operation.
[assumes A-30377-2]

label.description: `Baseline__c.Name`. Over 80 characters is a 400, not a 500.

cutDateTime.description:
Optional; defaults to the server clock. Becomes `resolutionTimePoint` in the response.
**Never accepted in the future** (`ASOF_IN_FUTURE`) — a baseline of content that does not
exist yet is not a baseline.

The request keeps MVP-30030's caller-facing name; the response returns the two timestamps
that name splits into.

resolutionTimePoint.description: What the baseline resolves against. **Stamped once, never re-derived.**

takenAt.description: The wall-clock moment of the cut. Kept apart from `resolutionTimePoint` so a clock correction cannot change what a baseline resolves to.

memberCount.description:
How many rows the cut resolved, **excluding tombstones**. This is the count of what the
configuration *contains*, not the count of rows the tree endpoint renders. Also the
canary behind `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT`; `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` is fed by the
`claiming`-row count recorded alongside it.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** The cut also records a count of
> explicitly pinned rows, feeding `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT`. Like the `claiming` count, it is
> stored and **not** returned here: there is no `pinnedCount`. [assumes A-30375-3]

resolutionTimePoint.description: What the baseline resolved against when it was cut.

rows.description:
The re-resolved rows, reusing the tree shape so clients render both the same way — with
`edgeId` and `edgeKey` nulled, `governingTimestamp` collapsed onto this baseline's own
`resolutionTimePoint`, and excluded rows filtered out.

warnings.description:
**Drift only** — `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` and `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT`. Mixed-revision
and collision warnings from the underlying resolution are not forwarded.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30375, not yet implemented.** A third drift code,
> `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT`. [assumes A-30375-5]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` is **not**
> forwarded here: it is advice about the branch, not drift. [assumes A-30376-2]

EntryKind.description:
What kind of change the diff found. Deliberately framed in generic framework terms (source /
member / claim) rather than MBOM terms, so the taxonomy survives a second
configuration-item type. See the preview endpoint's table for the full catalog.

Decision.description:
Whether this entry needs the caller to decide anything. **Only two values** — there is no
third, optional-but-defaultable tier. The only decision point anywhere in a pull is disposing
an orphaned claim; everything else, including new, removed and colliding upstream content,
applies automatically.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Still two values. An `informational`
> entry may now **offer** an optional action in `availableActions`, and the default when
> none is sent is today's outcome. `required` still means `claim-orphaned` only: a pull
> has exactly one required kind. [assumes A-30378-10]

Action.description:
An action the commit endpoint can apply. Both values only ever apply to `claim-orphaned`;
a decision naming any other kind is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`.

- `convert-to-native` — sever the claim's provenance link, keeping its branch-owned
  content, which then resolves on the branch clock. ("Native" is the framework's existing
  term for branch-owned content with no upstream provenance.)
- `remove` — append a deletion marker (an exclude delta). Nothing is hard-deleted.
- `accept-source-revision` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Offered
  only on `claim-retained` with `retargeted: true`, and optional. The commit pins the
  claim to the **candidate's** revision through a `set-revision`, never an `update`. The
  claim keeps its quantity and find number, and stays pinned. The decision carries
  nothing but `entryId` and `action`. [assumes A-30378-3, A-30378-11]

- `accept-fields` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Optional, on
  `claim-retained` and `member-add-collision`. It takes the fields named in
  `acceptedFields`, and the rest keep the branch's values. On `claim-retained` it equals
  `accept-source-revision` when the only accepted field is
  `childItemRevisionId: candidate`, and both are accepted. It compiles to **one**
  operation per row, never two on one edge:
  - `update` for `quantity` / `findNumber` alone
  - `set-revision` for the revision
  - `set-revision` carrying the quantity or find number too, when both are accepted

  [assumes A-30379-1, A-30379-5, A-30379-6]
- `release` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Optional, on
  `claim-superseded` only, where the claim now matches upstream anyway. It is the conscious
  way to stop holding a value. On a **pinned** claim it clears the revision, and the claim
  stays, tracking. On a **tracking** claim it releases the claim itself, compiled as a
  `revert`, and the row falls back to `base`. Takes no `acceptedFields`.
  [assumes A-30379-3]

| Value | Status |
|---|---|
| `convert-to-native`, `remove` | ✅ shipped — `claim-orphaned` only |
| `accept-source-revision` | 🚧 MVP-30378 — today it answers `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| `accept-fields`, `release` | 🚧 MVP-30379 — today they answer `INVALID_REQUEST` |

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** A decision is valid when its entry
> **offers** its action in `availableActions`, instead of only on `claim-orphaned`.
> [assumes A-30378-11]

branchId.description: The owning branch, denormalised for display.

sourceType.description: Only `Ebom` is in scope for Phase 1; `Pull` (branch-to-branch) is reserved.

candidateSourceVersion.description: Absent or null when `hasChanges` is false and no newer revision exists to preview.

hasChanges.description:
False when the branch already resolves against the candidate, or there is no newer
released revision. `entries` is empty in that case. **Not an error condition.**

entries.description:
Every difference found, in a stable, deterministic order. Always present; empty rather
than absent.

warnings.description:
Non-blocking conditions about what would render *after* the pull — typically `MIXED_REVISION`, and `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` for a branch edit a post-pull pin will hide. Always present; empty rather than absent.

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30376, not yet implemented.** `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` is not
raised here. The branch tree read is the one that raises it. [assumes A-30376-2]

truncated.description:
True when the **informational** entry set exceeded `entriesLimit` and was trimmed.
Entries with `decision: required` are never truncated. `summary` still reflects the
untrimmed totals.

entriesLimit.description: The effective cap applied this call — the query param, or the server default of 200.

diffFingerprint.description:
Opaque `sha256:`-prefixed digest of the inputs and the **complete** resolved entry set
(not the truncated page). Echo it back on commit; a mismatch means the world moved in
between and fails fast with `STALE_REVISION`.

It covers a **clock-free** projection of the entries, because a claiming row's
`governingTimestamp` *is* the read clock — folding it in would make every commit stale on
arrival.

generatedAt.description: Server clock at computation time. Informational; **not** a resolution input, and not part of the fingerprint.

SourceVersionRef.description:
One version of a source — the accepted eBOM root revision plus the clock that governs
traversal beneath it.

> **Known genericity tension.** `rootItemRevisionId` / `rootItemNumber` / `rootRevisionLabel`
> are PLM-specific: they name an `Item_Revision__c`. Correct for a `Source_Type__c = 'Ebom'`
> source, the only type in Phase 1 scope. When a second source type is implemented, make this
> schema a `oneOf` discriminated on the `sourceType` already present on `PullPreview` — an
> additive change, not a rewrite.

sourceRevisionId.description: The `Branch_Source_Rev__c` recording this acceptance. **Null on `candidateSourceVersion`**, which does not exist until a commit creates it.

resolutionTimestamp.description:
**T_R** — the timestamp the eBOM traversal resolves against. Stamped once at acceptance
from the root revision's release date and read thereafter, never re-derived. Deriving it
per-read would let a later corrected or backdated approval silently rewrite history.

acceptedAt.description: Wall-clock moment the acceptance was committed, kept distinct from `resolutionTimestamp`. Null on `candidateSourceVersion`.

DiffSummary.description: Counts over the **untruncated** entry set, so a caller can render "N informational, M requiring a decision" without walking `entries`.

required.description: Entries that will block a commit until given an explicit decision. Only `claim-orphaned` counts here.

byKind.description: Count per `EntryKind`, keyed by kind. Kinds with no entries are omitted.

entryId.description:
Stable, opaque handle, passed back to the commit endpoint to attach a decision. A
**deterministic hash of `kind` plus the correlation key** — never a database Id, never
positional, never generated — so recomputing the same diff yields the same ids. Treat it
as opaque; do not parse it.

availableActions.description:
Empty except on `claim-orphaned`, whose two dispositions are the only actions this API offers anywhere.

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Also `[accept-source-revision]` on a
`claim-retained` entry with `retargeted: true`. It is optional: the entry's `decision`
stays `informational`. [assumes A-30378-3, A-30378-10]

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** Optional per-field decisions on three
kinds. `claim-retained` gains `accept-fields`, beside `accept-source-revision` when
retargeted. `member-add-collision` gains `accept-fields`. `claim-superseded` gains
`release`. Every other kind is unchanged. [assumes A-30379-7]

retargeted.description:
**Present only on `claim-retained`; `null` on every other kind** (deliberately not
defaulted — a `false` would assert something about a kind for which the question is
meaningless).

True when the suppressed upstream change was a **re-target**: the candidate would resolve
this edge to a different child *revision* than the claim renders — the shape a
**pinned** claim takes when upstream re-revs its line. False when only field
values (quantity, find number) were suppressed. Lets a caller filter for the
higher-stakes case — a branch silently keeping a superseded revision after upstream moved
on — without parsing `message`.

The child *revision*, not the child *item*: see the endpoint description.

**🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** A `true` here is what makes the entry
offer `accept-source-revision`. [assumes A-30378-3]

revisionAdvances.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Present on `claim-retained` and
`claim-superseded`, and `null` on every other kind, deliberately not defaulted, like
`retargeted`.

`true` when this is a **tracking** claim, one that stores no revision, and the revision
it renders moves with this pull: after the commit it renders the candidate's line
revision. The entry's kind is still judged on quantity and find number alone. The
move is otherwise visible only by comparing `current.detail.childItemRevisionId` with
`candidate.detail.childItemRevisionId`.

**Never true together with `retargeted`.** `retargeted` is about a *pinned* claim that
upstream moved away from. A pin does not move, so its `revisionAdvances` is `false`.
A tracking claim is never retargeted. The value is covered by `diffFingerprint`.
A `base` row's advance is still `member-version-advance`, unchanged.

claimKind.description:
Present on `claim-*` kinds; null elsewhere. Distinguishes a claim created by
**claiming** an upstream edge from one created by **replacing** it. Both dispose
identically; this exists so the UI can explain what is being orphaned.

*Was `overrideKind` before MVP-30309 (breaking).*

message.description: Human-readable, already-localized summary. Never parse it — switch on `kind`.

current.description: How the branch renders this member today. **Null for `member-added`.**

candidate.description: How it would render after the pull. **Null for `member-removed`**, and for a `claim-orphaned` resolved by `remove`.

MemberTarget.description: Identifies what the entry is about, independent of before/after state.

edgeId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` for this member. Null for `base` content, which has no branch-owned record until something claims it.

edgeKey.description:
The **display** key — `Assembly_CI__c.Edge_Key__c` / the legacy `Assembly__c` line id.
**Not** what a pull correlates on: it moves when a parent item revs, which is exactly why
the diff cannot join on it.

label.description:
Short display label for the member — the **child item's** item number
(`Item__c.Name`). On a `source` target it is the root item's number instead, because
that entry is about the root item and has no child.

path.description: Breadcrumb from the root to this member's parent, for UI context.

PathSegment.description: One ancestor in a breadcrumb. Same shape as `MemberTarget` minus the path — a segment never nests its own breadcrumb.

MemberState.description: A member as resolved at one point in the diff (before or after). The generic fields are framework-level; everything type-specific lives in `detail`.

AssemblyEdgeDetail.description:
**The one MBOM-specific schema.** Everything above this point is reusable framework
vocabulary; this is the single place assembly/BOM concepts appear. A second
configuration-item type becomes a sibling schema in `MemberState.detail`'s `oneOf` and
changes nothing else.

## The three name fields are null on a tree read

`parentItemNumber`, `childItemNumber` and `childRevisionLabel` are populated **only on the
diff paths** — the pull preview and the comparisons. Those build a name cache with a
repository read of their own; the tree reads deliberately do not pay for one, so they return
all three as `null`. Treat them as optional display sugar, never as evidence that an item has
no number. The identity and content fields beside them are populated everywhere.

parentItemId.description:
The owning **item**, not its revision. `Assembly_CI__c` carries no parent-revision lookup
at all: a local edge's parent item is stable across revision advances while its parent
revision is not — and `Edge_Key__c` is unique org-wide, so two branches claiming the same
eBOM line share one row, meaning every field on it must be branch-invariant.

**Null on a root entry** — see `quantity` for why.

parentItemNumber.description: Null on tree reads — see the schema description.

childItemNumber.description: Null on tree reads — see the schema description.

childItemRevisionId.description:
The child revision this row renders. Which clock chose it depends on the row, and the
enclosing `governingTimestamp` does not always name that clock:

- a `base` row resolves at the source's T_R, and `governingTimestamp` is T_R;
- a **tracking** claim (no stored revision) also resolves at T_R — it renders the source
  line's revision — but its `governingTimestamp` is `asOf`, because that one field also
  governs the claim's quantity and find number;
- a **pinned** row (a stored `childItemRevisionId`, MVP-30357) renders the pin whatever
  either clock says; its `governingTimestamp` is `asOf`, which chose nothing;
- a floating `new` row or substitute, and every `nested` row, resolve at `asOf`.

A tombstone over a source line keeps the revision of the line it removed; a tombstone of
a branch-local row carries none. Also null on a floating row whose item has nothing
released at `asOf` — the row still renders.

This is the value to send back as `childItemRevisionId` to pin, or keep, what the tree
shows.

childRevisionLabel.description: Null on tree reads — see the schema description.

quantity.description:
**Null on a root entry.** The `source-version-advance` / `root-version-differs` entry at
the top of a pull diff or comparison is about the root *item*, which has no parent, no
quantity and no find number — its `target.ciKind` is `source`, not `assembly-edge`. Every
edge entry populates all three.

findNumber.description: A Salesforce `Number` field, never a string. **Null on a root entry** — see `quantity`.

candidateRootRevisionId.description: The released root revision being accepted. Same validation as the preview's query param — and re-validated here, from the re-resolved diff.

diffFingerprint.description: Echoed back from the preview this commit is acting on. A mismatch against the freshly re-resolved diff fails the whole commit with `STALE_REVISION`.

decisions.description:
One entry per `claim-orphaned` entry from the preview. **Every one must appear**, or
the commit is rejected with `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED`; naming any other kind is rejected
with `INVALID_REQUEST`. Send `[]` (or omit) when the preview had no required entries.

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** It may also carry **optional**
> decisions: `accept-source-revision` on a retargeted `claim-retained` entry. These are
> never required, and an entry left undecided keeps today's outcome.
> `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` still keys on `claim-orphaned` alone. [assumes A-30378-10]

> **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** It may also carry `accept-fields`
> (with `acceptedFields`) on `claim-retained` / `member-add-collision`, and `release` on
> `claim-superseded`. These are optional too. [assumes A-30379-7]

entryId.description: An `entryId` from the preview this commit is acting on.

childItemRevisionId.description:
`convert-to-native` only (MVP-30357): the child revision to **stamp** onto the
converted row. Same meaning and validation as `DeltaOperation.childItemRevisionId`
on a `convert-to-native` operation, which this is copied onto. "Keep what it
shows" is the orphaned entry's own `current.detail.childItemRevisionId`, sent
back. Ignored on `remove`.

trackChildRevision.description:
`convert-to-native` only (MVP-30357): `true` stores no revision, so the converted
row floats at the read clock like an `add`. A `convert-to-native` decision carries
**exactly one** of this and `childItemRevisionId`, or the commit answers
`422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` before any delta or acceptance is written. Ignored
on `remove`. **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** Also ignored on
`accept-source-revision`, whose revision is always the candidate's.
[assumes A-30378-11]

acceptedFields.description:
**🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** `accept-fields` only, and
required there. Each key is a field of the entry and each value says what to do
with it. **Name only what you are taking.** An omitted field keeps the branch's
own value, which is today's outcome.

| Value | Meaning | Stores |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate` | Hold what upstream resolves now | the candidate's value. For the revision this is a **pin**, which reports `retargeted: true` again when upstream next moves the line. |
| `release` | Stop holding the branch's own value | nothing. For the revision this is the state `trackChildRevision: true` leaves. A claim becomes a tracking claim that follows T_R and still gets a `claim-*` entry on every pull. A native row (`member-add-collision`) floats at the read clock. |

`candidate` and `release` render identically on this pull and differently on
later ones.

Refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`:

- any key other than the three below, including `childItem` and the old spelling
  `childItemRevision`
- an empty object
- a field that does not **actually diverge**, meaning the value the branch holds
  does not differ from the candidate's. A tracking claim holds no revision, so
  its revision never diverges, even when `current` and `candidate` render
  different revisions.
- `release` on a value the branch does not hold
- `release` on `quantity` or `findNumber`, which have no clock to fall back to.
  Use `revert`, or `release` on `claim-superseded`.
- `acceptedFields` on any action other than `accept-fields`

[assumes A-30379-1, A-30379-2, A-30379-7]

newSourceRevisionId.description: The `Branch_Source_Rev__c` this commit created — an **insert**, never an update.

applied.description:
Every entry that took an explicit decision, plus every `claim-retained`,
`claim-superseded` and `member-add-converged` outcome — the set a caller needs to
reconcile its held preview against what actually happened. (Re-previewing immediately
after a commit is always `hasChanges: false`, so this is the only place to learn it.)

`member-add-converged` reports `action: "retired"`; see the endpoint description.

AppliedEntry.description:
One outcome the commit is reporting back. Four kinds appear here and no others:
`claim-orphaned` (the decision you supplied), `claim-retained` and
`claim-superseded` (informational), and `member-add-converged` (retired by the commit).

A re-preview straight after a commit is always `hasChanges: false`, so this array is the
only place the retained and superseded outcomes can be read.

kind.description:
| Value | Status |
|---|---|
| `claim-orphaned`, `claim-retained`, `claim-superseded`, `member-add-converged` | ✅ shipped |
| `member-add-collision` | 🚧 MVP-30379 — only when an `accept-fields` decision was taken on it |

[assumes A-30379-8]

action.description:
What was done:

- `convert-to-native` or `remove` — the decision supplied for a `claim-orphaned`
  entry.
- `retired` — on `member-add-converged`. The commit appended a `Revert` delta dropping
  the branch's now-redundant local assertion. No decision is accepted for this kind.
- `null` — on `claim-retained` and `claim-superseded`, where nothing was written.
- `accept-source-revision` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30378, not yet implemented.** On a
  `claim-retained` entry that took that optional decision. The claim is now pinned to
  the candidate's revision. [assumes A-30378-11]
- `accept-fields` / `release` — **🚧 Planned — MVP-30379, not yet implemented.** On the
  `claim-retained`, `member-add-collision` or `claim-superseded` entry that took that
  decision. [assumes A-30379-8]

edgeId.description: The branch-owned `Assembly_CI__c` this entry's target names, if any.

CompareSideKind.description:
Which resolution produced a side of a comparison. The right-hand side may be any of the
four; the **left** may only be `branch` or `baseline`, because those are the two objects a
comparison path is rooted at.

Sent as `rightKind` — where it is matched case-insensitively — and returned as
`left.kind` / `right.kind`, always in this lower-case spelling.

CompareKind.description:
What a comparison entry reports. The counterpart to `EntryKind`, which is the **pull's**
vocabulary, and deliberately a separate set: a pull is asymmetric and its kinds name what a
pull would *do*, while a comparison is symmetric and does nothing. `member-added` and
`member-removed` are the two wire values the two vocabularies share, and they mean the same
thing in both.

See the endpoint description for what each one means and when it is emitted.

Comparison.description:
The whole answer to "how do these two configurations differ": what each side was, one entry
per differing correlation key, counts over the complete set, and each side's own warnings.

No envelope, nulls not suppressed, and every collection always `[]` rather than absent —
the same conventions as the rest of this API.

left.description: The side the path named — a branch or a baseline.

identical.description:
True when the two configurations contain the same members with the same content.

Derived from the entry list rather than from the summary: true exactly when no entry of
any kind other than `member-unchanged` is present. So it reads the same whether or not
the unchanged rows were asked for, and a `root-version-differs` entry is enough on its
own to make it false.

entries.description:
One entry per differing correlation key — plus every matching one when
`includeUnchanged=true` — ordered by breadcrumb path, then find number, then child item
id, then kind. Always present; empty rather than absent, and empty is the ordinary
shape of an identical comparison.

leftWarnings.description:
Warnings about the **left** side's own resolution — typically `MIXED_REVISION` — plus
`COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER`, which is about the pair and is reported here, first, because it
reframes everything below it.

Split per side rather than by adding a `side` field to `TreeWarning`, which would put a
new null key on every existing tree endpoint's warnings.

rightWarnings.description: Warnings about the **right** side's own resolution. Always present; empty rather than absent.

truncated.description:
True when `entries` was capped at `entriesLimit`. The cap is a plain prefix and
`summary` still reports untruncated totals, which is what makes this actionable.

entriesLimit.description: The effective cap applied this call — the query parameter, or the server default of 200.

generatedAt.description:
Server clock at computation time, read **once** for the whole call so the two sides are
never resolved microseconds apart. Not a resolution input — each side publishes its own
clocks.

ComparisonSide.description:
One of the two configurations that were compared: what it was, how it resolved, and on
which clock.

Published for **both** sides rather than echoed only for the one the path named, because a
comparison's answer is unreadable without knowing what was compared — `member-added` means
nothing until the reader knows the right side is a baseline from March rather than the
branch's own source.

id.description: The record this side was addressed by — a `Branch__c`, `Baseline__c`, `Branch_Source__c` or `Item_Revision__c`.

label.description:
The side's own display name where the addressed record has one — `Branch__c.Label__c`
for a branch, `Baseline__c.Name` for a baseline — and the **root item number** otherwise,
so a UI always has something to render beside the column. A `source` and an `ebom` side
are named by what they supply rather than by a record a user would recognise.

rootRevisionId.description: The root `Item_Revision__c` this side resolved to. **Null** when a source has nothing accepted yet.

asOf.description:
The read clock this side was resolved at — the caller's `asOf` / `rightAsOf`, the
server clock when none was supplied, an eBOM revision's release date, or a baseline's
frozen `Resolution_TimePoint__c`. A baseline echoes the timepoint its **cut** recorded,
which makes it obvious the caller could not have chosen it.

sourceTimePoint.description:
**T_R** — the timepoint this side's `base` content resolves at. Separate from
`asOf` because that is the whole model: a side reporting one number could not explain
its own rows.

An `ebom` side publishes the same value in both, honestly rather than leaving this null:
a raw walk has no acceptance pinning it and no branch content floating above it, so its
traversal clock **is** its T_R. Null only where a source has accepted nothing.

CompareEntry.description:
One difference between the two configurations, keyed by correlation key.

**Not the pull's `DiffEntry`.** That contract names its two states `current` and
`candidate`, which is a lie on a symmetric pair — a baseline compared against a raw eBOM has
no "current" side — and it carries four fields a comparison has no use for. The **leaf**
types are shared deliberately: `MemberTarget`, `MemberState`, `PathSegment` and
`AssemblyEdgeDetail` describe where a member sits and how one side renders it, which is
identical work in both features. Only the envelope differs.

entryId.description:
Stable, opaque handle: a deterministic hash of the kind plus the correlation key,
truncated to 16 hex characters. Never a database id, never positional, never generated —
so a repeated comparison returns the same handles. There is nothing to pass it back to;
it exists so a client can key a row. Do not parse it.

**One entry per correlation key, always** — two entries on one key would collide, which
is why `member-differs` carries `differingFields` rather than splitting into one kind
per field.

differingFields.description:
Which of the three assertable values disagree, in a fixed order so two calls produce
byte-identical lists. Populated on `member-differs`; **empty on every other kind** —
empty rather than null, so a client can iterate unconditionally.

Provenance is deliberately not among them: each side's state already publishes it, and
a provenance-only difference is not a content difference.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label, with the member's own item number appended. Translated; switch on `kind`, never on text.

left.description: How the **left** side renders this member. **Null on `member-added`.**

right.description: How the **right** side renders this member. **Null on `member-removed`.**

CompareSummary.description:
Counts over the **whole** comparison, never over a truncated entry list.

Read the two groups differently. `total` and `byKind` count entries **emitted**, so both
move with `includeUnchanged`. `added`, `removed`, `differing` and `unchanged` count
correlation keys and do not.

total.description: Entries produced — `root-version-differs` and any `member-unchanged` included. Moves with `includeUnchanged`.

added.description: Correlation keys present on the **right** side only.

removed.description: Correlation keys present on the **left** side only.

differing.description: Correlation keys present on both sides whose content disagrees.

unchanged.description:
Correlation keys present on both sides and identical.

**Populated whether or not `includeUnchanged` was set**, which is the point of it: the
default comparison emits no row for an identical member, and a caller still needs to
know how much of the configuration matched without paying for the rows. It therefore
does **not** always equal `byKind['member-unchanged']`, which counts emitted entries and
is `0` by default.

byKind.description:
Count per `CompareKind`, keyed by its wire value, over emitted entries.

**Pre-seeded with all five kinds at zero**, unlike the pull's `DiffSummary`, which
carries only the kinds it observed: a comparison is read by a client rendering a fixed
set of counters, and an absent key would make each one a null check.

RestError.description:
The MBOM's error shape. Keyed **`code`**, not the framework's `errorCode`.

A 403 body carries the label **only**: naming the object a caller was just denied would hand
them the schema they have no access to. It goes to the debug log instead. A 500 *does* carry
the exception type and message — an unmodelled fault has to be diagnosable and its caller is
our own UI or an integration — but never the stack trace.

code.description:
The stable error code. Every value below is a client error; a 500 carries
`INTERNAL_ERROR`, which is listed here for completeness but is not a code to branch on.

message.description:
The Custom Label for `code`, with a parenthesised **detail** appended naming the specific
row or value. The label says what went wrong and what to do about it; the detail says
which row it happened to. Translated — never parse it.

failures.description:
Present **only** on an atomic delta batch that failed validation. Carries the complete
per-operation failure list, so a caller does not have to find their faults one round trip
at a time.

Forbidden.description:
`FORBIDDEN` (403). The caller lacks an object grant this endpoint requires. The body names no
object — see `RestError`.

A field-level denial deeper in the stack is also answered 403: under `USER_MODE` that
surfaces as a `QueryException`, and every query on this path is built from a fixed field
list, so an access failure is far and away the likeliest cause.

value.message: You do not have permission to perform this action.

NotFoundPath.description:
`NOT_FOUND` (404). The path id is absent, unparseable, or names a **different object** than
this endpoint expects — the last of which is why swapping a `branchId` for a `sourceId` is a
clean 404 rather than a 500 out of a repository.

Also answered for any unrecognised trailing segment: `GET .../branches/{id}/bogus` is the
MBOM's own 404 in the MBOM's own shape (`code`), not the framework's (`errorCode`).

|---|---|---|
| `STALE_REVISION` | `diffFingerprint` mismatch, or an `entryId` that no longer names an entry in the freshly re-resolved diff | re-run `pull-preview` and resubmit |
| `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` | a `claim-orphaned` entry has no decision | supply one for every required entry |
| `NOT_RELEASED` / `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER` | revalidated at commit time and no longer qualifies | pick another candidate |

PullUnprocessable.description:
422 — well formed, but impossible against the model. Retrying the identical request will
never succeed.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH` | the candidate belongs to a **different root item** than the source |
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` / `EBOM_CYCLE` | a cycle in the eBOM below the candidate root |
| `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` | the correlation join cannot tell which upstream line corresponds to which branch line — one of the three shapes below |
| `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | *commit only* — a `convert-to-native` decision carried neither or both of `childItemRevisionId` and `trackChildRevision: true` |
| `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH` | *commit only* — a `convert-to-native` decision's `childItemRevisionId` is not a revision of the row's child item |

`AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` is raised in three shapes. Which remedy applies depends on the
shape, and the message's detail names the edges involved:

1. **A genuine duplicate line.** Two edges on the **same side** share a correlation key
   **and** a parent revision. This is data: the BOM has to change, by giving one of the
   lines its own secondary unique key — unless the pair is two of the branch's own rows
   at one key, which a branch edit clears.
2. **A pairing that would be a guess.** Edges at one key are left on **both** sides under
   different parent revisions, with more than one on a side. Usually data; a branch row in
   the mix can be removed to clear it.
3. **Two unpaired edges at one position.** Two or more edges at one key (bar `nested`
   rows) would be left without a counterpart on **one** side, where the diff could report
   only one of them. For example, a `replace` substitute beside a claim on a line of the
   same child that upstream drops, or an orphaned claim beside one. A branch edit clears
   this: exclude the substitute, or dispose of or remove one of the claims.

One parent item rendering at two revisions is **not** one of these: the parent revision
separates those lines.

That revision belongs to a different item than this branch's source. Choose a revision of the same root item. (a0Ag8000000Ab77EAC)
This change would make the child an ancestor of its own parent, which no BOM can represent. (beneath Assy-100 rev-2 at edge Harness-011)

ComparisonConflict.description:
409 — well formed, and retryable once state changes.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `NOT_RELEASED` | `rightKind=ebom` names a revision that is not Released, or is Cancelled, Expired, or carries no release date |

The same four-part test an MBOM's creation and a pull both apply, and a 409 for the same
reason: releasing the revision makes the identical request succeed. A Draft revision never
appears at any timepoint and has no release date to pin a walk to, so there is nothing to
compare against.

ComparisonUnprocessable.description:
422 — well formed, but impossible against the model. Retrying the identical request will
never succeed.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` | the correlation join cannot tell which member on one side corresponds to which on the other. The same three shapes, with the same remedies, as on the pull (see `PullUnprocessable`): two edges on one side sharing a key **and** a parent revision, edges at one key left on both sides under different parent revisions with more than one on a side, or two or more edges at one key left unpaired on one side. One parent item rendering at two revisions is not one of them |
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` | a cycle in the eBOM beneath either side's root, so that side cannot be resolved at all |

Both sides are resolved, so either can raise either code. `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION`'s detail
names the offending side in the **comparison's** own vocabulary — `left side`,
`right side`, or `right and left sides` — where a pull's says `current` and `candidate`.
The label before it is shared with pull-preview; switch on `code`, and read the ids rather
than the nouns.

A comparison always reports a cycle as **`CYCLE_DETECTED`**, never as the traversal's own
`EBOM_CYCLE`: the two mean the same thing to a caller and are both 422, and carrying the
inner code out would make this contract depend on which internal walk happened to find it.
A tree read, which has one walk and no such choice, still answers `EBOM_CYCLE`.
